title: Title: Adaptive Quantum State Collapse for Quantum Simulation
abstract: Quantum simulation, the process of mimicking the behavior of quantum systems, holds immense promise for advancing scientific discovery in fields ranging from materials science to drug discovery. However, traditional quantum simulation methods often face challenges related to computational cost and fidelity, particularly when simulating complex systems with intricate dynamics. This paper introduces an adaptive quantum state collapse mechanism designed to address these limitations. We propose a reinforcement learning-based approach to dynamically adjust collapse criteria for quantum states, optimizing for both simulation accuracy and computational efficiency. The core mechanism utilizes a feedback loop that continuously assesses the system's internal state and adjusts collapse thresholds to achieve a balance between fidelity and resource utilization. We demonstrate the efficacy of this approach through simulations of a simplified, yet representative, system exhibiting dynamic quantum correlations. The resulting algorithm offers a potential pathway to significantly enhance the performance of quantum simulations.

title: Messages Passed Along the Edges: A Interdisciplinary Mapping Review of Graph Neural Networks for Relational Data
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of Graph Neural Networks for Relational Data in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of GNN and graph learning as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: Beyond the Buzz: How to implement AI in Sport Science and Practice
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is frequently presented as a near-universal solution for all tasks and problems in professional sport. However, the term is applied inconsistently, often functioning as a label for considerably simpler computational methods. Following Russell and Norvig's (2021) definition of AI as encompassing reasoning, decision-making, and problem-solving, this talk argues that successful adoption depends less on acquiring advanced algorithms than on organizational readiness, governance, and collaboration. Drawing on several national AI-readiness frameworks (NIST, 2023; Ontario Government, 2023; NSW Department of Customer Service, 2024) and recent practitioner guidance for sport leaders, the talk outlines three decision points organizations should address before wide ranging AI implementation. First, clarifying the motivation of the implementation and thereby distinguish adoption driven by genuine performance or hopeful efficiency gains from adoption driven by fear of missing out. Second, defining the scope of the implementation which requires deciding whether AI should be applied organization-wide or excluded from ethically sensitive domains such as athlete health data. This also includes weighing the interpretability of "black box" models and clarifying who remains accountable for AI-informed decisions. Third, assessing the impact of the implementation, which requires benchmarking AI-supported processes against existing practice in terms of efficiency and cost, while considering potential negative effects on staff expertise or athlete–coach interaction. The talk further addresses implementation-level challenges that might hinder the use of AI tools. To put these general ideas in perspective, practical interdisciplinary applications are presented of collaborations projects with the Dutch short track speed skating national team. The projects were both part of the last two Olympic cycles and helped the national by optimizing training scheduling and relay performance. Lessons learned on cooperative implementation are presented and contrasted with the aforementioned guidelines. Taken together, while AI offers substantial potential for professional sport and sport scientists, organizations are encouraged to resist reactive adoption in favor of a deliberate AI action plan, supported by adequate staff literacy and strategic external partnerships. This includes a call for leaders in the sport domain to actively shape rather than merely react to AI's growth while keeping athlete welfare central to decision-making. The overarching message is to embrace AI, but with a clear plan for how and for whom. References National Institute of Standards and Technology. (2023, January 26). AI risk management framework. title: Исследование применения искусственного интеллекта в мессенджерах как инструмент автоматизации продаж и взаимодействия с клиентами
abstract: Тема выпускной квалификационной работы: «Исследование применения искусственного интеллекта в мессенджерах как инструмент автоматизации продаж и взаимодействия с клиентами». Использование чат-ботов в этом контексте позволяет бизнесу решить сразу несколько задач: обеспечить мгновенный первичный отклик, снизить нагрузку на менеджеров, стандартизировать качество коммуникаций и собирать данные о клиентах в автоматическом режиме. Особую роль здесь играют технологии больших языковых моделей (Large Language Models, LLM), которые позволяют чат-ботам понимать запросы в свободной форме и давать содержательные, а не шаблонные ответы. Актуальность данного исследования определяется следующими факторами. Во-первых, рынок чат-ботов растёт стремительно: по оценкам аналитиков Grand View Research, мировой рынок чат-ботов к 2030 году превысит 27 млрд долларов при среднегодовом темпе роста около 23%. Во-вторых, в России данная технология всё ещё остаётся относительно новой для малого и среднего бизнеса - большинство компаний либо не используют боты вовсе, либо ограничиваются простыми кнопочными сценариями без ИИ. Это создаёт значительное конкурентное преимущество для тех, кто внедряет интеллектуальные боты уже сейчас. В-третьих, доступность API крупных языковых моделей (OpenAI, Yandex GPT, GigaChat) сделала внедрение ИИ-ботов реалистичным даже для небольших компаний.

title: Bridging the Gap
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is a pervasive force influencing decision-making across healthcare, education, finance, law, and creative industries. While AI enables significant efficiencies and innovations, its growing use raises profound concerns about transparency, fairness, accountability, and potential harm. These concerns intensify when AI systems operate as “black boxes,” whose complex internal processes are not easily interpreted. The recent advent of generative AI (GenAI) introduces new challenges and opportunities, underscoring a critical need for understanding their operational dynamics. This chapter explores the evolution of AI from foundational principles to cutting-edge GenAI advancements, highlighting their burgeoning roles in modern societal systems and educational environments. A central theme is the indispensable importance of explainability. Explainable AI (XAI) ensures that decisions and content generated by AI systems can be understood, evaluated, and contested by human users and stakeholders. This imperative for clarity is especially vital in sensitive, high-stakes contexts such as healthcare and education. We present compelling real-world examples illustrating the detrimental impact of AI bias, including algorithmic discrimination in hiring and credit assessment, and discuss GenAI “hallucinations” where models confidently fabricate false information. To mitigate these challenges, key explainability techniques are introduced, including SHAP, LIME, feature attribution, counterfactual reasoning, and prompt tracing, demonstrating how these methods enhance human trust, user agency, and effective oversight. Furthermore, comprehensive ethical frameworks for responsible AI development are outlined, elaborating on five interconnected principles: transparency, fairness, accountability, privacy, and user autonomy. The chapter advocates for a human-centered approach envisioning GenAI as a collaborative partner in learning and creativity, guided by robust ethical standards and mechanisms for transparency and control, empowering stakeholders to leverage AI responsibly and meaningfully.

title: Sentiment Analysis in NLP
abstract: From rule-based systems to deep learning, the author presents everything you need to know about sentiment analysis As sentiment analysis evolves from simple lexicon matching to sophisticated multimodal deep learning, practitioners need authoritative guidance spanning the field’s entire trajectory. Sentiment Analysis in NLP delivers this breadth, covering text-based, aspect-based, multimodal, and implicit sentiment analysis, integrating text, audio, and visual data processing while addressing both theoretical foundations and real-world implementations. This book examines neural network architectures including CNNs and RNNs for text analysis, transformer models like BERT, and Graph Attention Networks. Dedicated chapters cover attention mechanisms and generative AI for synthetic data generation. Practical applications span product development, social media monitoring, and public health surveillance. Python code, datasets, and a solutions manual support hands-on learning. Readers will also find: Multimodal sentiment analysis techniques integrating text, speech, and image data to interpret emotional content across diverse communication formats Transformer-based models and attention mechanisms including BERT and GPT architectures that have transformed state-of-the-art sentiment classification performance Real-time context-aware sentiment analysis systems designed for continuous monitoring applications in social media and business intelligence environments Ethical considerations addressing data privacy, algorithmic bias, and transparency challenges that practitioners face when deploying sentiment analysis systems Case studies demonstrating sentiment analysis applications across customer feedback analysis, public safety monitoring, and healthcare decision support contexts This reference serves NLP researchers, data scientists, and business intelligence professionals who implement sentiment analysis systems. Graduate students in machine learning and deep learning will find both theoretical depth and practical resources for coursework and research applications.

title: EyeMakeYou: Identity-, Task-, and Subjective-State-Conditioned Diffusion for High-Frequency Gaze Synthesis
abstract: Eye movement biometrics (EMB) is an emerging behavioral modality for user authentication, particularly in virtual- and augmented-reality systems, where gaze dynamics contain distinctive subject-specific features. However, robust EMB systems require diverse, high-quality gaze recordings that are expensive to collect and often unavailable at the scale needed for model development. Generative models can mitigate data scarcity, but existing methods either synthesize generic gaze behavior or personalize signals primarily by identity, without jointly representing the user's task and subjective state. Consequently, generated signals may appear visually realistic while failing to retain the behavioral properties required for biometric applications. To address this limitation, we propose EyeMakeYou, a multi-conditional denoising diffusion framework for subject-specific, high-frequency gaze synthesis. EyeMakeYou generates 5-s, 1000-Hz bivariate gaze-velocity sequences from an identity-removed reference trajectory and conditions the denoising process on an identity embedding, a task embedding, and self-reported ratings of overall difficulty, mental tiredness, and eye tiredness. Its objective combines diffusion noise prediction and identity preservation with multi-resolution spectral, drift-consistency, and event-weighted local-smoothness losses. Experiments on GazeBase show that EyeMakeYou achieves higher median spatial accuracy and greater real--synthetic similarity in the embedding feature space than the existing generative approaches, while retaining selected task-dependent associations between subjective reports and oculomotor features. These findings support conditional diffusion as a practical approach for augmenting gaze datasets for biometric and interactive applications.

title: Vanilla Exact Synthesis of CNOT Circuits is NP-hard
abstract: Exact CNOT synthesis seeks a minimum-size circuit implementing a given invertible binary linear transformation. We study its vanilla formulation: synthesis from the identity on fixed labeled qubits, without ancillas and with all-to-all connectivity. We prove that this problem is NP-hard and that its bounded decision version is NP-complete. Hardness persists even for unitriangular targets that are low-rank perturbations of the identity and under near-linear gate budgets. Our proof gives a polynomial-time reduction from the NP-complete Hamiltonian path problem on grid graphs. A unary hypercube embedding translates graph vertices into circuit parities and edge traversals into CNOT updates. The central challenge is that Hamiltonian paths require intermediate vertex visits, whereas exact synthesis constrains only the final transformation. We bridge this gap with a replicated recorder qubits construction that encodes the required parities in the final outputs, together with a tight gate budget that forces every sufficiently short implementation to trace a Hamiltonian path. Crucially, this path structure is enforced by the construction rather than imposed as a restriction on the circuit. The result directly implies NP-hardness for shortest word problem and Cayley-graph distance computation over $\mathrm{GL}(n,2)$ with elementary transvections as generators, as well as fixed-width sequential XOR program minimization. For CNOT-minimal exact phase polynomial synthesis, it yields NP-hardness with a zero phase polynomial; extending the reduction to grid-graph Hamiltonian cycle problem establishes hardness even when the final linear transformation is the identity. These complementary results show that the linear and phase components each independently suffice for NP-hardness of exact phase polynomial synthesis.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Phase Estimation with Photon-Added Even and Odd Coherent States in an SU(1,1) Interferometer
abstract: We investigate phase estimation in an SU(1,1) interferometer employing $m$-photon-added even and odd coherent states as nonclassical input resources. The phase sensitivity is evaluated through intensity detection and the error propagation method, while the ultimate precision limit is determined from the quantum Cramér-Rao bound with the quantum Fisher information serving as the relevant metrological quantity. Our results demonstrate that photon addition significantly enhances the phase sensitivity, increases the quantum Fisher information, and reduces the quantum Cramér-Rao bound, leading to a clear improvement over the corresponding even and odd coherent states. Furthermore, the achievable sensitivity exceeds the standard quantum limit and gradually approaches the Heisenberg scaling with increasing photon-addition number. We also find that the $m$-photon-added even coherent states exhibit a modest advantage over their odd counterparts. As $m$ increases, however, this distinction becomes progressively weaker, suggesting that photon addition diminishes the role of the initial parity of the coherent state in determining the interferometric performance.

title: Fresh Memory, Stale Plans: Derivation Currency for Distributed LLM-Agent Memory
abstract: A large language model (LLM) agent that inherits a plan through shared memory can hold the latest requirement yet act on a plan derived from an older one: fresh memory, stale plan. Freshness checks miss this failure because they compare local copies with current state (observation currency) rather than the inputs the plan was derived from (derivation currency). Planfence makes derivation currency checkable after a handoff. Stored plans carry exact links to their recorded inputs; before a protected action, Planfence follows those links to an action-specific dependency frontier, asks each input's owner for its current head, refreshes what changed, and allows one replan before blocking. Application code supplies the links and declares the scope; no shared memory service is required. Holding the native S-Bus validator fixed, supplying inherited input versions raises detected handoff conflicts from 0/30 to 30/30: retained evidence is the missing ingredient. In 30 live five-agent workflows with a revision inserted after planning, a freshness-only executor acts on the stale plan every time, whereas Planfence, like a centralized-lineage baseline that requires a shared store, completes all 30 correctly. In matched replay under emulated LTE traces, Planfence's stall stays within 143-237ms per action across a 64$\times$ range of update rates while per-update synchronization grows from 52 to 1196ms; synchronization is cheaper only at the lowest tested rates. Scoping queries to the declared dependencies holds traffic at 8.1KiB per action, a tenth of all-key validation at 128 keys; at full scope the two tie.

title: Non-Linear Random Matrix Dynamic Encoding
abstract: This paper investigates the application of Non-Linear Random Matrix Dynamic Encoding (NLRM) to enhance model generation and feature extraction. Traditional random matrix encoding often suffers from static representations, limiting its ability to capture dynamic changes crucial for optimal model performance. NLRM offers a novel approach by dynamically encoding the matrix, allowing for continuous adaptation and optimization. We present a comprehensive framework for implementing this technique and demonstrate its efficacy through illustrative examples involving a simulated regression problem. This work highlights the potential of this method to significantly improve model accuracy and generalization. The core mechanism centers around the continuous, adaptive encoding of the non-linear random matrix, leading to improved feature extraction and enhanced model performance.

title: Quantum Phase Matching: Dynamic Pattern Matching for Enhanced Computation
abstract: Quantum phase matching (QPM) is a powerful technique in quantum computing that involves carefully aligning the phase of a quantum state with a target state. This technique has emerged as a crucial tool for enhancing the performance of quantum algorithms, particularly in areas like quantum simulation and optimization. title: Title: Quantum Entanglement Network Propagation for Information Transfer
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a cornerstone of quantum mechanics, offers the potential for unparalleled information transfer capabilities. However, maintaining and extending entanglement over long distances presents a significant challenge. This paper explores a novel protocol for quantum entanglement propagation, designed to optimize for speed and fidelity of information transfer through the implementation of a dynamically-adjusted entanglement network. We introduce a mechanism that facilitates the propagation of entanglement through a network, increasing the rate of information transfer compared to traditional methods. This work addresses the fundamental limitations of existing approaches and lays the groundwork for a robust and scalable quantum information network. The proposed protocol employs a hierarchical network structure and incorporates adaptive entanglement distribution strategies to enhance robustness and efficiency. We present a detailed mathematical framework, including key operational parameters and performance metrics, demonstrating the efficacy of our approach in a simulated environment. The resulting network demonstrates a significant improvement in information transfer rate and fidelity compared to baseline models. This research contributes to the advancement of quantum communication and information processing technologies.

title: 基于动态自适应的深度学习的特征选择
abstract: The selection of features is a fundamental and critical step in deep learning models, significantly influencing their performance and generalization ability. Traditional feature selection methods often rely on predefined rules or heuristics, which can be inflexible and suboptimal when faced with varying data distributions. This paper proposes a novel deep learning framework, termed "Dynamic Adaptive Feature Selection" (DAFS), that dynamically adjusts feature selection strategies based on real-time data input changes. We leverage a feedback loop to iteratively refine the feature selection process, leading to enhanced model robustness and improved generalization performance. The DAFS framework demonstrates a significant improvement in accuracy and robustness compared to conventional methods across a diverse range of datasets. This work introduces a mechanism to dynamically adjust the selection process, ensuring optimal feature representation for each data point.

title: Quantum Key Distribution Protocol Optimization based on Entangled States
abstract: This paper investigates the optimization of Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) protocols utilizing entangled states. The core claim is that strategic optimization of entangled state generation and utilization can significantly enhance the security and key rate of QKD. The proposed method leverages principles from quantum information theory and entanglement theory to design a protocol that maximizes key distribution speed while minimizing the risk of key leakage. Current QKD protocols predominantly rely on single photons, often neglecting the full potential of entangled states. This work addresses this limitation, aiming to improve the efficiency and security of quantum key distribution. The presented protocol incorporates techniques for enhanced entanglement distribution, error correction, and privacy amplification, all tailored for maximizing key rate within a secure framework. Mathematical analysis and theoretical considerations are detailed throughout, outlining the protocol's operational parameters and security proofs. The ultimate goal is to demonstrate a more robust and efficient approach to QKD based on the fundamental properties of entanglement. ---

title: Information-Theoretic Metrics for Neural Network Robustness
abstract: This paper investigates the application of information-theoretic concepts, namely entropy and mutual information, to assess the robustness of neural networks. Traditional methods for evaluating robustness often rely on gradient-based approaches, which can be misleading and fail to capture the full complexity of vulnerability to adversarial attacks and noise. We propose a novel framework that leverages entropy and mutual information to quantify the information flow within a neural network. Specifically, we introduce metrics based on the entropy of activations and the mutual information between input perturbations and output changes. These metrics provide a more granular and accurate representation of robustness compared to gradient-based measures. Our approach offers a fundamental shift in how we understand and measure robustness, potentially leading to the development of more resilient and reliable neural networks. The core idea is that robustness isn't simply about the magnitude of gradients, but about the *information* that an adversary can effectively transmit to cause a change in the network's output.

title: Quantum-Inspired Randomized Search for Algorithm Design
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to randomized search algorithms, termed Quantum-Inspired Randomized Search (QIRS). The core premise is that the principles of quantum superposition and interference, traditionally associated with quantum computing, can be effectively translated into classical algorithms to enhance their efficiency. The proposed methodology involves representing candidate solutions as quantum states and utilizing interference patterns to strategically guide the search process. This departs from traditional randomized search which relies solely on random sampling, introducing a layer of probabilistic control mimicking quantum behavior. The effectiveness of QIRS is evaluated through theoretical analysis and conceptual demonstrations, highlighting the potential for significant improvements in algorithm design, particularly in complex, high-dimensional search spaces. We demonstrate a shift in the search strategy from purely stochastic exploration to a more informed, interference-driven process. The key contribution lies in adapting quantum concepts to optimize the exploration process within randomized search, offering a new direction for algorithm design and optimization.

title: Quantum Decoherence-Based Quantum Computing Error Correction Code
abstract: This paper proposes a novel quantum computing error correction code predicated on the principles of quantum decoherence. The core concept leverages the inherent fragility of quantum states to create a robust error detection and correction mechanism. Specifically, the code aims to control and manipulate the decoherence time of individual qubits, utilizing this temporal constraint within a structured error correction scheme. The theoretical framework details the encoding, decoding, and error correction processes, incorporating mathematical formulations to quantify the redundancy introduced and the resulting improvement in qubit fidelity. The proposed code's effectiveness is demonstrated through simulations, showcasing its potential to significantly enhance the reliability of quantum computations, a critical step towards achieving scalable quantum computing. The key contributions lie in the direct integration of decoherence dynamics into the error correction strategy, offering a fundamentally different approach compared to traditional methods. The paper concludes with a discussion of potential optimizations and future research directions.

title: Title: Adaptive Topology for Machine Learning
abstract: Adaptive topology for machine learning aims to enhance model performance and robustness through dynamic adjustment of neural network connections and layers. This paper introduces a novel framework that learns to optimize the network's topology during training, driven by data-driven feedback. We propose a method that utilizes a reinforcement learning agent to iteratively adjust the network's structure, leading to improved generalization and resilience to noisy data. The core mechanism involves learning a 'topology map' that guides the network's growth, allowing it to effectively capture complex relationships within the input data. This contrasts with traditional methods that rely on pre-defined topologies, offering a potentially more flexible and effective approach to machine learning. The study demonstrates the effectiveness of this approach through extensive experiments on a variety of benchmark datasets, showcasing significant improvements in accuracy and stability. The framework is designed to be easily adaptable to different neural network architectures and data types.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Constraint Satisfaction with Bayesian Optimization
abstract: Quantum-enhanced constraint satisfaction problems (CSPs) offer the potential for significant speedups compared to classical approaches, particularly for large and complex CSPs. This paper investigates a novel quantum-enhanced strategy for solving CSPs, utilizing a quantum annealer to efficiently explore the solution space and identify optimal configurations. We introduce a Bayesian optimization framework tailored for this application, integrating quantum annealing to accelerate the search process and improve solution quality. The core mechanism centers on leveraging quantum annealing to identify promising regions of the search space, guided by Bayesian optimization, resulting in significantly reduced computational cost and enhanced solution accuracy. The paper details the implementation of the quantum annealer, Bayesian optimization algorithm, and the resulting performance evaluation on a benchmark CSP. The results demonstrate a substantial improvement in solution finding time and solution quality compared to classical approaches, highlighting the potential of this quantum-enhanced strategy.

title: FieldMind AI (GFM): An AI-Powered Operational Intelligence Platform for Field Service Businesses
abstract: Field service businesses — including pool service, HVAC, and pest control operators — typically manage complex, safety-sensitive, and time-critical operations with limited administrative staff and fragmented software tooling. This whitepaper presents FieldMind AI (GFM), an AI-powered operational intelligence platform designed to unify communication, compliance monitoring, inventory tracking, and decision support for small and mid-sized field service companies. GFM combines workflow orchestration, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), and a vector-based knowledge layer to convert routine operational signals — chemical readings, equipment alerts, inventory levels, and customer messages — into structured, actionable intelligence. We describe the system architecture, its eight functional modules, and preliminary findings from an early beta pilot conducted with an independent field service operator. We conclude with a discussion of the platform's technical contributions and its applicability within a field service management software market projected to grow at a compound annual rate in the double digits through the early 2030s.

title: Analisis Sentimen Ulasan Produk Skincare Sephora Menggunakan Algoritma Bert
abstract: The rapid growth of the skincare industry has made consumer reviews a crucial factor in purchasing decisions. However, the massive volume of reviews on platforms like Sephora makes efficient manual analysis difficult. This study aims to develop and evaluate an automated sentiment analysis system to classify Sephora skincare product reviews into positive, negative, and neutral categories using the Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) algorithm. The research methodology applies a modified CRISP-DM framework. A dataset of 4,687 reviews was collected through crawling from the X (Twitter) platform for the period of January 2025 to January 2026. The data was cleaned into 4,683 tweets, pre-labeled using the VADER lexicon, and split with an 80:20 ratio for training and testing data. The modeling process was conducted through fine-tuning the bert-base-uncased model for 3 epochs. Experimental results demonstrate that the BERT algorithm achieved the highest performance with an accuracy of 91%, precision of 90%, recall of 89%, and an F1-score of 90%. This performance significantly outperforms baseline methods such as VADER (72% accuracy) and Naive Bayes (78% accuracy). The sentiment analysis successfully extracted consumer perception patterns; positive sentiment was dominated by service recommendation reviews, while negative sentiment focused on price complaints and product side effects. The BERT prediction results showed 2,756 tweets (58.9%) of positive sentiment, 975 tweets (20.8%) of negative sentiment, and 952 tweets (20.3%) of neutral sentiment. This pattern is consistent with the initial VADER label distribution. This research provides practical recommendations for consumers, Sephora, and manufacturers in understanding market preferences and optimizing business strategies.

title: MAXIMIZAÇÃO MULTIOBJETIVO DA APRENDIZAGEM UTILIZANDO O ALGORITMO RLCO PARA OTIMIZAÇÃO DA PROFICIÊNCIA E RETENÇÃO COGNITIVA
abstract: This study presents the development and validation of an integrated mathematical model for optimizing study schedules in adaptive tutoring systems, termed the Unified Objective Function of Learning. Traditionally, computerized educational systems approach knowledge management in a fragmented manner, focusing isolatively on proficiency measurement, mnemonic retention, or operational efficiency. The methodology proposed here fills this gap in the literature by unifying three competing theoretical strands within a Learning Assessment Interface: the psychometric modeling of latent traits via Item Response Theory (IRT), the exponential decay of memory based on Ebbinghaus’ Forgetting Curve, and the mitigation of temporal effort governed by Wright’s Learning Curve. To mediate the intrinsic biological and economic conflict among these forces—where deep learning demands time and time constraints limit learning—a weighted additive utility function was constructed, subjected to operational constraints of maximum cost and biological consistency. The resolution of the resulting non-linear, hyperdimensional search space was mapped using the RLC Optimizer (RLCO) algorithm, a recent Metaheuristic grounded in the electromagnetic phenomenology of alternating current electric circuits. In the proposed model, the cost function acts as the active resistance (𝑅) of the medium, while the momentum of movement and the positional history of the agents are governed by inductive and capacitive reactances, respectively. The system regulates the intensity of the searchstep current through the Quality Factor (𝑄), ensuring a smooth transition between global scanning (exploration) and exact refinement (exploitation). Computer simulations based on 100 independentruns demonstrated that the RLCO converged with 100% feasibility to the stable global optimum, overcoming the local stagnation limitations of traditional algorithms. Scenario analysis evidenced the existence of a "perfect learning crest", where a balanced calibration of weights resulted in a schedule with an optimal review interval of approximately 4 days and a cap of 6 reviews, guaranteeing high levels of theoretical proficiency (~88,7%) and mnemonic retention (~79,8%) with a moderate time cost. The Learning Assessment Interface robustly solves the problem of endless or overlapping review schedules, paving the way for a new generation of adaptive tutors focused on maximizing human time efficiency.

title: STyMo: Fast and Controllable Few-Shot Motion Style Transfer
abstract: Supporting a wide variety of motion styles is critical for creating diverse virtual characters, but current methods either require large stylized datasets or pre-trained models that cannot generalize beyond their training distribution. We present STyMo, a few-shot approach that learns motion style from only seconds of paired data and trains in one to two minutes. Our key insight is to decompose style into two components: a static component capturing time-invariant posture, and a temporal component capturing frame-wise dynamics. This decomposition yields an interpretable system where posture intensity, temporal exaggeration, and per-body-region style can be adjusted at runtime. Furthermore, the reduction in required training data and computation time structurally permits an iterative authoring workflow. To ensure robustness on arbitrary inputs, we further introduce a stylizability gate that automatically prevents artifacts on out-of-distribution motions. We demonstrate results across diverse motion styles, from subtle emotional variations to exaggerated character archetypes, and release our processed paired dataset to facilitate future research.

title: Revisiting Topological Graphs for Macro Action based Closed-loop Reinforcement Learning of Vision Language Navigation in Continuous Environment
abstract: Vision-Language Navigation in Continuous Environments (VLN-CE) requires an agent to follow natural language instructions through unseen environments. Existing imitation learning (IL) pipelines struggle in this closed-loop setting: behavior cloning suffers from distribution shift, and DAgger's expert actions become ambiguous upon trajectory deviation. While Reinforcement Learning (RL) offers a natural paradigm to address this, directly applying RL to micro action spaces is sample-inefficient due to reward sparsity. To overcome this bottleneck, we reformulate VLN-CE as a Hierarchical Markov Decision Process (MDP), explicitly decoupling high-level planning from low-level control. By abstracting the environment into a topological graph, our high-level policy operates on a macro action space of frontier nodes, with a training-free low-level controller acting as its state transition, which significantly compresses the decision horizon and makes closed-loop RL tractable. To support RL optimization on the macro MDP, we propose an action-aware value head to effectively evaluate state values under the dynamic frontier action space, powering a graph-based PPO. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of our architecture. Finally, our model achieves state-of-the-art performance on the R2R-CE and RxR-CE benchmarks.

title: Building Pretraining Data for World Models: An Unreal Engine-Based Pipeline for Action-Conditioned Video Generation
abstract: Action-conditioned video models require large-scale visual data paired with control signals that are temporally aligned with the resulting scene transitions. Such supervision is difficult to obtain from ordinary real-world video because the actions that caused each visual change are typically unknown. We present a large-scale synthetic data production pipeline built on Unreal Engine for generating action-conditioned, multi-view video. To accommodate the different execution requirements of real-time physics and high-quality offline rendering, the pipeline executes trajectory generation and final rendering in two stages: Stage I runs real physics in PIE and records per-frame character states, control inputs, and camera states into an intermediate trajectory representation; Stage II replays those trajectories in a new engine process and renders them offline with Movie Render Queue (MRQ). Around this core, we develop a distributed production system with cache-aware task partitioning, node-local slot scheduling, automated scene screening, aesthetic and luminance filtering, partial-output recovery, asynchronous upload, and continuous cluster health monitoring. The production cluster contains 25 servers with eight NVIDIA RTX 5090 GPUs per server. From 2,384 asset packs, 429 levels were retained for production together with a pool of 40 humanoid characters. The pipeline has produced 2,691 hours of 1080p video and 6,076 hours of 720p video. We describe the system architecture, the implementation decisions that emerged from production failures, and the limitations of using perceptual quality proxies for world-model data curation. The pipeline described in this report constitutes the Unreal Engine synthetic-data production component used in EchoWM.

title: A Large Open Multi-Energy Corpus of Soil Compaction Tests, with Machine-Learning Baselines
abstract: Every engineered fill is specified by a maximum dry density and an optimum moisture content. Each determination needs a full Proctor test. Published correlations rest on one to four hundred specimens, usually from one laboratory at one compactive energy, and are seldom released. This paper releases a corpus without those limits. It holds 2,854 laboratory compaction tests from six public sources, across 162 provenance groups and four Proctor energy levels, with fines from 1.5 to 100%. Every record is audited to the Proctor method its source names, and no energy is inferred. Screening on the zero-air-voids condition removed 11.8% of harmonised records, and 5.7% of those with a measured specific gravity. A material share of published compaction data is physically impossible. The optimum degree of saturation over the corpus is 0.815 at a coefficient of variation of 11%. That is a baseline, not a constant. Both parameters are then estimated from one classification suite and the compaction standard. A tabular foundation model reaches R2 0.824 for density and 0.784 for water content under random folds. It reaches 0.727 and 0.696 with folds drawn around provenance, and 0.520 and 0.614 with a whole source held out. Compactive energy is negligible marginally yet decisive conditionally. Density on the 66 modified-Proctor records is predicted at R2 0.740 with it and -0.651 without. Symbolic regression yields closed forms coupled through a phase relation. No predicted pair can then exceed the zero-air-voids line. The predictions are for screening, not acceptance.

title: Quantum Potential-Based Adaptive Machine Learning Framework
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum potential-based machine learning framework designed to dynamically adjust model parameters for optimal performance. Traditional machine learning models often employ fixed parameters, limiting their ability to adapt to complex data. We propose a quantum mechanics-driven approach to model the relationship between input features and model parameters, allowing for adaptive parameter adjustments. This framework aims to surpass the capabilities of conventional machine learning by enabling a level of optimization unattainable through traditional methods. The core mechanism utilizes quantum entanglement and superposition to represent and manipulate the input space, facilitating a sophisticated and adaptive learning process. This research presents a framework that promises to enhance model accuracy, efficiency, and robustness.

title: Quantum Computing Based Geometric Optimization
abstract: Quantum Computing Based Geometric Optimization explores the potential of quantum algorithms to revolutionize optimization problems, specifically focusing on achieving enhanced efficiency compared to classical methods. This paper delves into the theoretical underpinnings and potential practical applications of this approach, emphasizing the unique capabilities offered by quantum computation in manipulating geometric data and solving complex optimization challenges. We present a framework for designing quantum-enhanced optimization algorithms, highlighting the key mathematical concepts and potential benefits across diverse domains. The core claim of this research centers on the utilization of quantum mechanics to significantly accelerate optimization processes, leading to improvements in computational speed and solution quality. The paper will outline the fundamental principles of quantum geometric optimization, detailing the advantages over conventional algorithms and exploring specific implementation strategies.

title: Title: Fractal Dimensionally-Induced Constraint Optimization (FDCO)
abstract: Fractal Dimensionally-Induced Constraint Optimization (FDCO) presents a novel optimization algorithm that leverages fractal geometry to generate complex, optimized geometries. Traditional optimization methods often struggle with complex, non-uniform constraints, necessitating iterative refinement and potentially inefficient search spaces. FDCO addresses this challenge by employing a fractal-based constraint system that iteratively refines a design, creating self-similar patterns that automatically enforce specific structural properties. This approach allows for the discovery of highly optimized and intricate designs, surpassing the limitations of conventional methods. This paper explores the theoretical foundation, implementation details, and preliminary results demonstrating the effectiveness of FDCO in generating complex geometries.

title: Self-Correcting Neural Networks via Adaptive Error Feedback Loops
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to neural network training—self-correcting neural networks—based on the incorporation of adaptive error feedback loops. The core idea is to leverage the network's own prediction errors not just for gradient updates, but as a driving force to refine its parameters and actively detect and mitigate systematic biases. Traditional backpropagation relies on a static error signal, often failing to address underlying issues that lead to persistent inaccuracies. Our proposed method introduces a cyclical feedback system, allowing the network to continuously monitor its performance, identify deviations from the desired output, and adjust its internal parameters to minimize these deviations. This approach mimics biological feedback mechanisms and promises improved learning efficiency, robustness, and accuracy, particularly in scenarios with complex or noisy datasets. We detail the architecture, the feedback loop implementation, and a theoretical framework for understanding the convergence properties of these networks. The key innovation lies in the dynamic adjustment of the feedback parameters, creating a self-regulating learning process. The presented system demonstrates potential for achieving superior performance compared to standard training methods, especially when dealing with problems characterized by high variance or systematic errors.

title: Bayesian Network for Hyper-Dimensional Data Clustering
abstract: This paper explores the application of Bayesian Networks (BNs) to hyper-dimensional data clustering, aiming to surpass existing methods in accuracy and interpretability. Hyper-dimensional data presents significant challenges for traditional clustering techniques, demanding robust and understandable representations. We propose a novel BNN architecture that dynamically adapts to the data distribution through a latent space representation, guided by Bayesian inference. The core mechanism involves learning a probabilistic network that effectively interprets the data, leading to superior clustering results. The paper details the BNN's architecture, training process, and evaluation on a benchmark hyper-dimensional dataset, demonstrating its superior performance compared to state-of-the-art methods. Finally, we discuss the limitations and potential future directions of this approach.

title: Generative Adversarial Networks for Cryptographic Protocol Design
abstract: The design of secure cryptographic protocols is a notoriously difficult and time-consuming endeavor, often relying heavily on expert intuition and manual analysis. This paper proposes a novel approach utilizing Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) to automate and potentially accelerate this process. The core idea is to frame protocol design as a two-player adversarial game. A generator network, tasked with designing cryptographic protocols, competes against a discriminator network, which evaluates the generated protocols for vulnerabilities against known attacks. Through iterative adversarial training, the system learns to produce increasingly secure protocols. We outline the architecture of this GAN system, detail the training methodology, and discuss potential applications and future research directions. The primary goal is to shift from a largely manual, reactive design process to a more proactive, data-driven approach, ultimately leading to more robust and efficient cryptographic protocols. We define a key security metric, *E*, representing the expected success rate of an attacker against a given protocol, and utilize this metric within the GAN's loss function. The generated protocols are evaluated using simulations and formal verification techniques, and the discriminator learns to accurately predict the *E* value.

title: Semantic Quantum Entanglement Computation
abstract: This paper explores the potential of leveraging quantum entanglement for efficient computation and storage of semantic information, encompassing concepts and their relationships. The core claim is that utilizing quantum entanglement allows for parallel and distributed processing of semantic data, surpassing the limitations of classical computers in understanding and retrieving semantic information. The proposed mechanism involves encoding semantic information within entangled quantum states and manipulating these states through quantum gates to facilitate parallel computation and rapid exploration of complex relationships. This research represents a novel approach by integrating quantum computing with semantic understanding, offering a pathway to overcome traditional computational bottlenecks in semantic reasoning and information retrieval. The presented framework demonstrates a theoretical foundation for a new paradigm in information processing, focusing on exploiting quantum phenomena for enhanced semantic data manipulation. The key mathematical concepts and operations employed are outlined, providing a foundation for further research and development in this field. ---

title: Quantum Information Cryptography Protocol Design
abstract: Quantum information cryptography offers the potential for unprecedented security through the use of quantum mechanics. This paper presents a novel quantum information cryptography protocol designed to establish unbreakable encryption utilizing entanglement and quantum error correction principles. We explore a quantum key distribution (QKD) protocol that incorporates a novel error correction mechanism based on quantum error correction principles. The design focuses on creating a robust and resilient encryption system capable of resisting known attacks. The proposed protocol utilizes entanglement to generate a shared secret key, which is then protected by a quantum error correction mechanism. This paper details the protocol's architecture, error correction strategies, and potential security implications.

title: Decentralized Quantum Sensor Networks with Byzantine Fault Tolerance
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to building robust and reliable decentralized quantum sensor networks capable of operating effectively even when confronted with Byzantine faults – malicious or faulty nodes intentionally disrupting network operation. The core of this system leverages quantum key distribution (QKD) for secure key exchange and incorporates advanced consensus algorithms to achieve Byzantine fault tolerance. The proposed mechanism guarantees data integrity and accuracy, mitigating the impact of compromised sensors. We detail the architecture, key components, and the theoretical underpinnings of this system, outlining a pathway towards practical, resilient quantum sensor networks. The key contributions of this work include the integration of QKD with Byzantine fault tolerance specifically tailored for sensor networks, offering a significant advancement over existing approaches that typically treat these challenges separately. Mathematical models and notation are presented for clarity and rigor.

title: Topological Protection of Quantum Decoherence
abstract: Quantum decoherence represents a significant hurdle in the development of practical quantum computers. The inherent fragility of quantum states makes them susceptible to environmental noise, leading to rapid loss of quantum information. This work explores a novel approach to mitigating decoherence by leveraging the principles of topological protection. We propose constructing a quantum bit (qubit) array utilizing a topologically protected architecture. This design aims to isolate qubits from unwanted interactions, thereby significantly reducing the detrimental effects of decoherence. The core mechanism relies on the robust nature of topological invariants, which shield the quantum states from local perturbations. This approach offers a promising pathway toward enhancing the coherence times of qubits and ultimately improving the reliability of quantum computation. The theoretical framework presented here outlines the design considerations and potential advantages of this strategy.

title: Relational Reinforcement Learning with Symbolic Representation
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to reinforcement learning (RL) that combines relational reinforcement learning (RRL) with symbolic representations. The core idea is to represent the state space using symbolic concepts derived from relational reasoning, providing a more structured and interpretable framework for learning. Traditional RL algorithms often struggle with generalization, particularly in complex, high-dimensional environments. By leveraging relational reasoning, we can capture underlying relationships between elements in the environment, leading to policies that are more robust and adaptable to unseen situations. This work details the architecture of the proposed system, including the symbolic representation learning module and the RL algorithm used for policy optimization. Empirical results, though not presented through experimentation, demonstrate the potential of this approach to improve both the generalization capabilities and the interpretability of learned policies. The key contribution lies in the integration of relational reasoning within an RL framework, offering a pathway towards more reliable and understandable intelligent agents. Specifically, we present a framework where the state is represented as a set of relations (s_1, s_2, ..., s_K) and these relations are used as input to the RL algorithm. We analyze the impact of different symbolic representations on the learning process and discuss future research directions.

title: Self-Adaptive Quantum Information Entropy Optimization Algorithm
abstract: Quantum information entropy is a critical parameter in quantum computation, and its optimization is essential for improving quantum algorithm efficiency. This paper presents a novel self-adaptive quantum information entropy optimization algorithm designed to dynamically adjust the entropy of quantum information, thereby enhancing quantum computation's performance. The algorithm leverages the dynamic evolution of the entropy and employs sophisticated optimization techniques to maximize the utility of quantum information. This research addresses a long-standing challenge in quantum computing – the need for robust and adaptable entropy control – and proposes a promising approach to achieve this goal. This work demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm through theoretical analysis and preliminary experimental validation, showcasing its potential for significant advancements in quantum information processing.

title: Adaptive Quantum Key Distribution Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces an Adaptive Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) algorithm designed to dynamically adjust key distribution strategies based on the current state of the key distribution. Traditional QKD algorithms rely on static parameters, limiting their adaptability and potential for improved security and efficiency. Our proposed algorithm leverages the inherent dynamic properties of quantum key distribution to automatically adjust key distribution based on observed key characteristics, offering enhanced robustness and operational performance.

title: Adaptive Probability Matrix Algorithm
abstract: This paper presents a novel Adaptive Probability Matrix Algorithm (APMA) designed to enhance the generalization capabilities of machine learning models. Traditional probability matrix methods often require manual parameter adjustments, limiting their effectiveness in handling complex data distributions. Our algorithm leverages deep learning models to automatically adjust the weight of the probability matrix, resulting in improved model prediction accuracy and robustness. We introduce a framework that dynamically adapts to data shifts, ensuring optimal performance across a wide range of scenarios. The core mechanism centers around a learned weight adjustment process, achieved through a deep neural network trained on data-driven insights. We detail the algorithm's architecture, training procedure, and empirical evaluation results, demonstrating its superior performance compared to existing methods. The paper concludes with a discussion of the implications of this approach for various machine learning applications.

title: Geometric Topology Quantum Graph Simulation (GTQGS)
abstract: The pursuit of understanding and manipulating geometric topology presents a significant challenge to computational science. Traditional methods often struggle to effectively simulate complex geometric structures due to the inherent limitations of classical computation. This paper introduces Geometric Topology Quantum Graph Simulation (GTQGS), a novel framework leveraging quantum computing to accelerate geometric topology simulation. We propose a quantum graph representation of geometric shapes, utilizing quantum algorithms to mimic the intricate topological properties of these shapes. The core mechanism of GTQGS lies in the direct and efficient simulation of geometric structures through quantum graph manipulation, offering a path towards significantly enhanced computational capabilities compared to existing approaches. This work addresses the limitations of classical simulation by introducing a fundamentally new approach to geometric topology, paving the way for more accurate and insightful modeling.

title: 自适应自组态算法的量子计算模拟
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to quantum computing simulation utilizing an adaptive self-assembly algorithm. Traditional quantum simulation methods often struggle to accurately model complex systems exhibiting self-organization, necessitating intricate parameter tuning and computationally expensive simulations. Our proposed algorithm dynamically adjusts simulation parameters based on observed system behavior, enabling a more efficient and potentially insightful exploration of system dynamics. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through the simulation of a simplified, yet representative, system with significant self-similarity. This work explores the potential of incorporating adaptive mechanisms to overcome limitations inherent in current quantum simulation techniques, highlighting a promising direction for advancing the field.

title: 基于量子计算的自适应机器学习模型训练
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of quantum computing to revolutionize machine learning, specifically focusing on the development of an adaptive machine learning model training algorithm. Traditional machine learning algorithms often struggle with high-dimensional datasets and complex non-linear relationships, limiting their scalability. Quantum computing offers the promise of significantly enhanced computational power through parallel processing, addressing these limitations. We propose a novel quantum-enhanced training algorithm that leverages quantum algorithms to accelerate the learning process, specifically targeting the improvement of model accuracy and generalization capabilities. The core mechanism centers around the application of quantum approximation algorithms to optimize the learning process, leading to faster convergence and improved performance on challenging datasets. The paper presents a conceptual framework, explores potential implementation challenges, and discusses future research directions.

title: Engineering a Two-Player Card Game in Godot 4 and GDScript: Architecture, Shader Design, and Artificial Intelligence Decision Making
abstract: This paper presents a software engineering case study on designing a reusable architecture for interactive 2D card games using Godot 4 and GDScript. Rather than focusing only on a specific game implementation, the study investigates generalizable engineering patterns for managing interactive objects, visual feedback, user interaction, and decision-making systems. A unified Item/Pool architecture is introduced to represent cards and game containers through reusable abstractions, reducing duplicated logic among different scene types. The proposed design separates input handling, object management, and rule enforcement through a signal-driven architecture. A canvas-item shader pipeline demonstrates how perspective tilt and dynamic shadow effects can be achieved in a 2D environment without requiring a 3D rendering pipeline. Furthermore, a transform-aware drop detection method based on affine inverse transformation is presented to overcome interaction errors caused by rotated interfaces. For opponent behavior, a deterministic rule-based artificial intelligence model is developed using weighted suit evaluation, legal-card filtering, and context-dependent card selection strategies. The results show that Godot 4’s scene instancing, typed GDScript, shader materials, and signal system provide suitable mechanisms for building maintainable interactive applications. The discussed solutions and engineering lessons can be applied to a broader class of UI-driven 2D games beyond card games.

title: A Deep Mixed-Image Augmentation Strategy for Few-Shot Image Classification
abstract: Few-shot image classification suffers from severe data scarcity and unstable generalization. Existing data augmentation strategies still have three major limitations: pixel-level fusion strategies are incompatible with the support–query structure of episodic learning, category selection for cropping-based augmentation is overly simplistic, and most approaches rely on a single augmentation method, limiting robustness. To address these issues, this study proposes a deep mixed data augmentation framework that jointly enhances both the support set and the query set. The method first performs global pixel-level fusion to construct fused support and query sets. A Hopfield network then turns fused-support similarities into a pairing matrix H, which assigns a different-class gallery partner for query-side cropping–mixing. Finally, cropping–mixing produces an enhanced query set for model training. The framework is validated using ResNet18+BDC as the backbone. Experimental results on MiniImageNet demonstrate that the proposed method is competitive in few-shot classification, attaining a five-seed test mean of 73.25%/81.88% under 5-way 1-shot and 5-shot. A single complementary run on FC100 attains 66.63%/77.80% and is not a same-backbone ranking against heterogeneous published protocols.

title: A soft-matrix symmetric cryptosystem with involutory keys for context-aware message encryption
abstract: Lightweight symmetric encryption increasingly serves short-message, resource-constrained systems where contextual data properties are operationally relevant. Ciphers such as Hill, AES, and DES treat plaintext as a uniform block, ignoring multi-attribute format. Soft set theory can parameterize such attributes, but most soft-set cryptosystems use nonstandard operators that hinder analysis and implementation. This paper introduces a symmetric key cryptosystem combining binary soft-matrix encoding with standard modular multiplication over Zm. Plaintext is represented as a soft matrix relating symbols to parameters (e.g. vowel/consonant class or ASCII parity), then encrypted with a self-invertible (involutory) key matrix. The involutory structure allows exact decryption with the same key, without matrix inversion, preserving algebraic transparency and computational simplicity. Algorithmic specifications and realistic short-message examples confirm exact decryption under an injective encoding. A Python prototype runs in tens of microseconds per message on a commodity CPU; a hardened timing harness (median, interquartile range) is released for reproduction on constrained targets. As a single linear round, the transformation offers intra-symbol but no inter-symbol diffusion, fails a NIST SP 800-22 subset, and, being deterministic, fails IND-CPA. Rather than rivaling modern nonlinear block ciphers, it offers a transparent, context-sensitive matrix architecture for controlled short-message use and cryptanalytic study. title: Machine learning for wind and solar PV energy production forecasting: a systematic literature review
abstract: Abstract The growing share of renewable energy, especially solar photovoltaic (PV) and wind, increases the need for reliable power production forecasts beyond the very short term. Medium-term horizons (here defined as forecasts of at least 24 h ahead) are important for planning tasks such as market bidding, reserve sizing, and operational scheduling, but research in this area is diverse and difficult to compare due to differences in horizons, datasets, and evaluation settings. This paper presents a systematic literature review of machine learning approaches for PV and wind production forecasting with horizons $$\ge 24$$ ≥ 24 h. Following PRISMA guidelines, a Scopus search using a broad query (2978 results), followed by a refined query (69 results) and a three-stage screening process (title, abstract, and full text), resulted in 31 included studies. We extract and synthesize evidence on (i) forecast horizons and setups, (ii) model families and hybrid designs, (iii) data sources and the use of measured versus forecast weather inputs, (iv) uncertainty handling (e.g., quantiles, intervals, and scenarios), and (v) links to decision-making contexts. In addition, we propose a taxonomy to classify studies along these dimensions and support comparison across different evaluation settings. The results show that most studies focus on day-ahead and week-ahead evaluation, while 2-week and longer horizons are less common. Hybrid and ensemble approaches are widespread, while transformer-family methods appear in a smaller but visible subset. Most papers rely on measured production data, whereas fewer explicitly use forecast weather (e.g., Numerical Weather Prediction) inputs, even though weather-forecast uncertainty strongly influences multi-day performance in realistic settings. Only a limited number of studies connect forecasts to operational decisions, indicating a gap between accuracy-focused evaluation and decision value. The review highlights the need for more consistent benchmarking, more realistic weather-input evaluation (and, where relevant, other operational exogenous inputs such as curtailment), and more standard uncertainty reporting for medium-term renewable forecasting.

title: Practical Applications of Sentiment Analysis
abstract: This chapter bridges cutting-edge sentiment analysis technologies with real-world impact by exploring how the field drives decision-making and innovation across three major domains: business intelligence, public safety and governance, and public health. It begins with business intelligence, demonstrating how enterprises transform massive volumes of customer feedback and social media data into strategic assets through the VoC framework and an emotion-driven decision-making loop covering brand reputation management, product innovation, competitor analysis, and precision marketing. A detailed case study on a global consumer electronics company's new product launch vividly illustrates the full process from real-time public opinion monitoring to rapid strategy adjustment. The chapter then examines applications in public safety and governance, where sentiment analysis serves as a societal emotional barometer for dynamic policy evaluation, social risk early warning, and smart emergency response, while addressing key ethical concerns such as power balance, algorithmic bias, and privacy protection. Finally, it focuses on public health, highlighting the use of sentiment analysis for real-time mental health trend monitoring, epidemiological intelligence during pandemics, and improving patient experience. A case study on the COVID-19 vaccination infodemic demonstrates how topic modeling combined with sentiment analysis can effectively combat misinformation and guide public communication. The chapter concludes with a technical deep dive into the unique challenges of social media sentiment analysis and a practical practitioner's guide comparing open-source tools, cloud APIs, and commercial SaaS platforms, providing clear selection criteria and implementation roadmaps.

title: The Natural Language Interaction Protocol and Standard for AI Agents
abstract: AI agents are increasingly being developed and deployed across organizations using heterogeneous agent-development frameworks, AI models, tool interfaces, protocols, and execution environments. To realize their potential social and business impact, these agents must be able to interoperate through a common communication protocol. The Natural Language Interaction Protocol (NLIP), developed by researchers and practitioners across companies and universities and standardized by Ecma International, addresses this need by defining a standards-based application-layer protocol for AI-agent interaction. NLIP provides a lightweight semantic message envelope that can be carried over existing transports such as HTTP/HTTPS, WebSocket, and AMQP, while allowing NLIP-aware agents and gateways to adapt between clients, agents, local context stores, ontologies, tools, enterprise services, and heterogeneous underlying protocols. This paper presents the motivation and design rationale of NLIP, its message model and transport bindings, security-by-design considerations, reference implementation, representative applications, adoption signals, and relationship to emerging agent protocols such as MCP and A2A.

title: WIDE: Wildcard Inference with Dynamic Expansion for Cross-Modal Generative Retrieval
abstract: Generative retrieval has demonstrated significant success by unifying representation learning and search into a single sequence-to-sequence generation task. However, extending this paradigm to cross-modal retrieval reveals a critical challenge arising from the inherent information asymmetry across different modalities, such as the gap between concise text queries and dense visual candidates. This structural mismatch causes the autoregressive decoder to suffer from forced hallucination when generating identifiers via standard trie-constrained beam search, where the model is severely penalized for failing to guess fine-grained details absent from the query, allowing irrelevant candidates to hijack top rankings. To address this issue, we propose Wildcard Inference with Dynamic Expansion (WIDE). WIDE employs Adaptive Entropy Thresholding (AET) to calibrate layer-specific uncertainty boundaries offline. During the decoding generation phase, Asymmetry-aware Wildcard Decoding (AWD) detects semantic blind spots and emits wildcards instead of forced deterministic identifiers, dynamically expanding the search space without incurring log-probability penalties. Finally, Blind-Spot Re-ranking (BSR) evaluates the expanded candidate pool using a hybrid scoring mechanism that combines discrete generation confidence with continuous semantic similarity. Extensive experiments on the M-BEIR benchmark demonstrate that WIDE outperforms state-of-the-art generative retrieval methods, effectively suppressing forced hallucination while maintaining compact index structures.

During the decoding generation phase, Asymmetry-aware Wildcard Decoding (AWD) detects semantic blind spots and emits wildcards instead of forced deterministic identifiers, dynamically expanding the search space without incurring log-probability penalties. Finally, Blind-Spot Re-ranking (BSR) evaluates the expanded candidate pool using a hybrid scoring mechanism that combines discrete generation confidence with continuous semantic similarity. Extensive experiments on the M-BEIR benchmark demonstrate that WIDE outperforms state-of-the-art generative retrieval methods, effectively suppressing forced hallucination while maintaining compact index structures.

title: Large-Language Models as a Cognitive Virus
abstract: Large-language models (LLMs) are rapidly becoming part of human culture, reshaping how information is produced, transmitted, and used. Here we propose that their diffusion can be understood through a viral analogy, with LLM use spreading through populations, becoming embedded in cognitive and cultural practices. We model transitions among uncoupled, coupled, and persistently dependent users, and show that the interplay between social transmission, recovery, and collective reinforcement can generate tipping points and technological lock-in. A central consequence is the possibility of runaway dynamics: once a critical threshold is crossed, small increases in adoption can trigger rapid population-level shifts toward persistent dependence, with abrupt losses in cognitive competence. The same framework, however, identifies conditions for cognitive immunization, based on reducing transmission and facilitating reversibility. Our results highlight how LLM adoption may involve nonlinear collective transitions with important consequences for cognitive autonomy.

title: Laplacian Frequency Hierarchies for Efficient 3D Gaussian Splatting Training
abstract: A key bottleneck in 3D Gaussian Splatting training is the continual growth of Gaussian primitives, which increases optimization cost and slows convergence, especially at high resolutions. We propose Laplacian Frequency Hierarchies, a simple yet efficient 3DGS scheme that combines Laplacian image decomposition with coarse-to-fine, frequency-staged training. After fitting lower-frequency structure, we archive the corresponding Gaussian field so that subsequent fields can optimize higher-frequency residuals without carrying the full primitive burden, and we compose the rendered components in the image domain via a Laplacian-style reconstruction at inference time. This design reduces the number of active Gaussians during training, thereby lowering optimization overhead and accelerating training. The proposed scheme is plug-and-play and orthogonal to prior 3DGS accelerations: it can be directly combined with strong backbones such as Taming-3DGS and FastGS to improve training speed with competitive reconstruction quality. It achieves average speedups of 1.73x and 1.21x at 1K setting, and 1.74x and 1.33x at 4K setting on Taming-3DGS and FastGS, with larger gains on more challenging scenes and increasingly pronounced benefits at higher resolutions.

title: 基于自适应的图神经网络的复杂性分析方法
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to complex network analysis, utilizing a dynamically adjusted graph neural network (GNN) to effectively assess the complexity of a given network. Traditional methods often struggle with evolving data and model characteristics, limiting their ability to capture intricate dependencies. We introduce a new algorithm, dubbed "Adaptive Complexity Analyzer," which employs a self-adaptive parameter adjustment strategy to continuously refine the GNN's representation, enabling improved performance across diverse complexity scenarios. The core mechanism involves learning a set of parameters that dynamically optimize the GNN's weighting and connectivity, fostering a more robust and adaptable model. This research directly addresses the limitations of static GNN architectures by introducing a framework for real-time complexity assessment. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach through a series of simulations and experiments, highlighting its superior performance compared to existing state-of-the-art methods in various complexity analysis tasks. The results indicate a significant improvement in the model's ability to accurately gauge network intricacy, leading to enhanced predictive capabilities.

title: Quantum Topology and High-Dimensional Data Compression
abstract: Quantum Topology offers a fundamentally new approach to data compression by leveraging the intricate properties of quantum geometry. This paper introduces a novel data compression technique based on quantum topology, demonstrating its potential to significantly enhance data transfer efficiency and storage space through the manipulation of high-dimensional data structures. The core mechanism involves mapping high-dimensional data to a lower-dimensional subspace using quantum algorithms, effectively compressing the data while preserving critical information. We present a preliminary analysis of the technique's performance and potential applications, highlighting its advantages over existing methods. This work establishes a foundation for exploring the transformative impact of quantum topology in the field of data compression.

title: Non-Euclidean Geometry and Quantum Computing: Adaptive Topology for Efficient Parallel Computation
abstract: This paper explores the integration of non-Euclidean geometry with quantum computing to achieve novel levels of parallel computation and adaptive topology. Traditional methods often struggle with complex geometric problems, limiting their applicability. We propose a novel framework leveraging quantum entanglement to establish a '拓扑桥接' mechanism, enabling the quantum computer to directly interact with and manipulate geometric structures. This approach holds the potential for significant advancements in computational efficiency and allows for self-adaptive topology, offering a pathway toward enhanced parallel processing capabilities. We detail the core mechanism, present the potential benefits, and outline future research directions.

title: Information-Theoretic Quantification of Neural Network Representations
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to analyzing neural network representations using information theory. Traditional methods often rely on empirical observations and subjective interpretations, lacking a rigorous theoretical basis. We propose a framework that leverages information-theoretic measures, specifically mutual information and entropy, to quantify the information content within the activations of hidden layers. This allows for a principled understanding of representational capacity, layer structure, and the potential for information bottleneck scenarios. The core of our approach is the formalization of neural network representation analysis through information theory, offering a new perspective on interpreting the learned features and their relevance to downstream tasks. We demonstrate the utility of this framework through conceptual analysis and illustrate how it can be extended to more complex network architectures. The proposed methodology provides a foundation for designing and training neural networks with enhanced representational properties and for understanding the underlying mechanisms of learning.
