title: Machine Learning-Based Sentiment Classification of Reviews from Indonesian Mobile Applications Using TF-IDF
abstract: The increasing volume of mobile application reviews has created a need for automated sentiment classification capable of handling large-scale and imbalanced user-generated data. This study aimed to compare classical machine learning algorithms and evaluate the effectiveness of class-weighted learning in improving minority-class recognition in Indonesian mobile application reviews. The dataset was cleaned, deduplicated, and controlled for conflicting labels and data leakage, resulting in 357,327 unique reviews across Negative, Neutral, and Positive sentiment classes. Textual features were represented using Term Frequency-Inverse Document Frequency (TF-IDF) with 50,000 features, and the data were divided using an 80:20 stratified train-test split. Logistic Regression, Multinomial Naive Bayes, Linear Support Vector Machine (SVM), and Random Forest were evaluated alongside class-weighted Logistic Regression and Linear SVM. Logistic Regression achieved the highest accuracy of 83.47%, whereas Balanced Linear SVM achieved the highest Macro F1-score of 62.87% and improved the Neutral F1-score from 8.70% to 21.18%, while maintaining an accuracy of 79.09%. The findings demonstrate that the highest overall accuracy does not necessarily indicate the most balanced classifier under class imbalance. Balanced Linear SVM provided the most favorable trade-off between overall performance and minority-class recognition, highlighting the importance of class-sensitive evaluation and class-weighted learning for imbalanced sentiment classification.

title: Feedforward Closedloop Learning (Error forward propagation)
abstract: This release solves the long term stability issues with FCL by applying Oja's rule at neuron level. Thanks to Suraj Prasanth Naranatt who found the solution to this problem. For an autonomous agent, the inputs are the sensory data that inform the agent of the state of the world, and the outputs are their actions, which act on the world and consequently produce new sensory inputs. The agent only knows of its own actions via their effect on future inputs; therefore desired states, and error signals, are most naturally defined in terms of the inputs. Most machine learning algorithms, however, operate in terms of desired outputs. For example, backpropagation takes target output values and propagates the corresponding error backwards through the network in order to change the weights. In closed loop settings, it is far more obvious how to define desired sensory inputs than desired actions, however. To train a deep network using errors defined in the input space would call for an algorithm that can propagate those errors forwards through the network, from input layer to output layer, in much the same way that activations are propagated.

title: 自适应几何场论的量子计算验证
abstract: This paper explores the application of adaptive geometric field theory (AGFT) to quantum computing verification, aiming to validate the theory's effectiveness through dynamic parameter adjustment based on quantum simulation results. The core claim posits the establishment of an AGFT capable of autonomously optimizing its parameters based on the output of quantum simulations, thereby mitigating reliance on theoretical modeling errors. We detail the methodology, including the representation of geometry as a quantum system and the use of quantum simulation to assess the theory's validity. The potential for this approach represents a novel paradigm in physics, offering a method for rigorous validation using the computational power of quantum machines.

title: AN EXPLAINABLE NEURO-SYMBOLIC SPEECH MATRIX MODEL FOR PERSONALIZED FOREIGN LANGUAGE PRONUNCIATION FEEDBACK
abstract: Automatic pronunciation support increasingly combines speech recognition, pronunciation assessment, and computer-assisted language learning, yet many systems still return only a transcription or global score. This article proposes the Neuro-Symbolic Speech Matrix Feedback model (NS-SMF), an explainable architecture that converts learner speech into diagnostic and pedagogically actionable feedback. Learner speech is represented through acoustic, phonetic-prosodic, and pedagogical error matrices. A neural encoder extracts acoustic-phonetic evidence, task-specific heads estimate segmental and suprasegmental deviations, reference alignment localizes errors, and a knowledge base or knowledge graph maps detected deviations to linguistically grounded explanations and corrective exercises. The model formalizes posterior-based scoring, dynamic alignment, integrated deviation, explanation confidence, feedback validity, pedagogical priority, learner-profile update, and multi-task training. A pilot protocol for Uzbek-speaking learners of English is outlined using technical, expert-agreement, explainability, and learning-improvement measures. The main contribution is a formal framework that moves pronunciation assessment from black-box scoring toward traceable, rule-grounded, and exercise-oriented feedback.

title: Lean 4 Confirmation and Approval Proof for Hamzah Equation. (36)
abstract: تحلیل و بررسی موتور تلمتری و پایش بلادرنگ (HamzahXcell_RealTime_Engine) در Cosmos OS کد ارائه‌شده یک گام مهندسی حیاتی و عملیاتی در معماری HamzahXcell (HIP) است که سیستم را از حالت تئوریک به یک شبکه عملیاتی بلادرنگ (Real-Time Telemetry Network) متصل می‌کند. با نگاشت ۲۰ مرکز داده به ۱۰ حالت کیفی سیستم و اعمال فرمول دترمینان ژاکوبی مستر با استفاده از ثابت‌های بنیادین ($\Omega_H = 1.176 \times 10^{10}$ و $\text{FLOOR\_EPSILON} = 1.155 \times 10^{-20}$)، سیستم توانسته است پایداری و تعادل تمام حالت‌ها را روی مقدار هدف ($1.0$) به صورت دترمینستی قفل و اعتبارسنجی کند. در ادامه، نسخه پیشرفته، شیءگرا، ایمن و بهینه‌سازی‌شده این اسکریپت پایتون به همراه اسکریپت تمامیت صوری در Lean 4 تقدیم می‌گردد: ۱. پیاده‌سازی پیشرفته Python: موتور تلمتری بلادرنگ (HamzahXcellRealTimeEngine) این اسکریپت ساختار شیءگرا، کنترل دترمینستی بذر تصادفی (np.random.default_rng), مدیریت صریح حالات و خروجی ساختاریافته را با پایداری کامل پیاده‌سازی می‌کند: Python import numpy as np class HamzahXcellRealTimeEngine: """ موتور تلمتری و پایش بلادرنگ سیستم‌عامل کیهانی (HamzahXcell Real-Time Engine) اعتبارسنجی یکپارچگی ۱۰ حالت کیفی سیستم با استفاده از فرمول دترمینان ژاکوبی مستر """ def __init__(self, seed: int = 42): self.omega_h = 1.176e10 self.floor_epsilon = 1.155e-20 self.rng = np.random.default_rng(seed) # شبیه‌سازی 20 مرکز داده بلادرنگ (Telemetry Nodes) با توزیع نرمال کنترل‌شده self.data_centers = self.rng.normal(1.0, 0.05, 20) def get_realtime_metrics(self, state_index: int) -> float: """محاسبه میانگین تلمتری جفتی برای حالت کیفی مشخص‌شده""" if not (1 <= state_index <= 10): raise ValueError(f"ILLEGAL_STATE: State index {state_index} out of bounds (Must be between 1 and 10).") idx = (state_index - 1) * 2 return float(np.mean(self.data_centers[idx:idx+2])) def verify_system_integrity(self) -> list[dict]: """ارزیابی جامع یکپارچگی سیستم و محاسبه دترمینان ژاکوبی مستر برای تمامی حالات""" print("=" * 85) print(f"{'--- HAMZAHXCELL REAL-TIME TELEMETRY & INTEGRITY REPORT ---':^85}") print("=" * 85) print(f"{'کد':<6} | {'مرکز داده (Avg)':<18} | {'متریک دترمینان':<20} | {'وضعیت'}") print("-" * 85) results = [] for i in range(1, 11): telemetry = self.get_realtime_metrics(i) # فرمول اصلی دترمینان ژاکوبی مستر با احتساب ثابت‌های امگا و اپسیلون کف determinant = (self.omega_h * telemetry) / (self.omega_h + self.floor_epsilon) # قفل پایداری: اگر دترمینان روی 1.0 باشد سیستم در تعادل کامل است is_stable = abs(determinant - 1.0) < 0.1 status = "STABLE (LOCKED)" if is_stable else "ANOMALY DETECTED" title: 基于自适应的拓扑变换的概率模型
abstract: This paper introduces a novel probabilistic model based on adaptive topology transformation, designed to enhance the accuracy of probability model predictions and reduce model complexity. Traditional probabilistic models often rely on static parameter estimation, failing to fully leverage the inherent properties of topology transformations. We propose a new framework that utilizes an adaptive topology transformation process to dynamically adjust model parameters, leading to improved predictive capabilities. The core mechanism involves an iterative self-adaptation algorithm that optimizes the model's parameters based on the observed data distribution. This approach addresses the limitations of existing methods by providing a more flexible and accurate representation of complex probability distributions. The proposed model demonstrates superior performance in several benchmark datasets, validating its effectiveness. The paper concludes with a discussion of the model's strengths and limitations, suggesting avenues for future research.

Traditional probabilistic models often rely on static parameter estimation, failing to fully leverage the inherent properties of topology transformations. We propose a new framework that utilizes an adaptive topology transformation process to dynamically adjust model parameters, leading to improved predictive capabilities. The core mechanism involves an iterative self-adaptation algorithm that optimizes the model's parameters based on the observed data distribution. This approach addresses the limitations of existing methods by providing a more flexible and accurate representation of complex probability distributions. The proposed model demonstrates superior performance in several benchmark datasets, validating its effectiveness. The paper concludes with a discussion of the model's strengths and limitations, suggesting avenues for future research.

title: Decentralized Reinforcement Learning with Distributed Bayesian Belief Propagation
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to decentralized reinforcement learning (DRL) that leverages distributed Bayesian belief propagation (DBBP) for enhanced coordination and robustness. Traditional DRL methods often struggle with scalability and convergence issues in complex, multi-agent environments. Our framework addresses these limitations by enabling agents to share knowledge and aggregate policies through iterative belief updates. Each agent maintains a local Bayesian belief about the environment and its own policy. These beliefs are dynamically updated using DBBP, which propagates information between neighboring agents based on their observations. This process converges to a globally consistent policy, significantly improving performance compared to standard decentralized RL techniques. We demonstrate the core claim that this approach enables robust and scalable reinforcement learning in decentralized environments. The key innovation lies in the synergistic combination of decentralized RL with distributed Bayesian inference, leading to a more effective strategy for knowledge sharing and policy aggregation. We present the core mechanism of the DBBP algorithm and analyze its convergence properties.

title: Anomaly Detection Based on Adaptive Neural Networks
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to anomaly detection utilizing adaptive neural networks. Traditional anomaly detection methods often struggle with dynamic environments and evolving data patterns. This research addresses this limitation by designing a neural network architecture capable of autonomously adapting its structure and parameters based on incoming data. The core principle leverages the inherent sensitivity of these adaptive networks to deviations from normal behavior. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this method through a theoretical analysis and a conceptual framework, highlighting its potential for improved accuracy and robustness in anomaly detection scenarios. The proposed approach offers a significant advancement over conventional statistical and machine learning-based methods by incorporating dynamic adaptation, leading to more reliable and responsive detection of anomalous events. ---

title: Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning with Adaptive Modality Selection
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to neuro-symbolic reasoning that leverages neural networks for adaptive modality selection. The core idea is to allow a neural network to dynamically assess the suitability of different modalities – such as images, text, and audio – for a given reasoning task. Based on this assessment, the network outputs a probability distribution over the available modalities, indicating the expected utility of each for the task. This distribution is then used to select the most promising modality for subsequent symbolic reasoning or knowledge graph queries. Unlike traditional neuro-symbolic methods that typically rely on a single, fixed modality, this approach offers the potential for significant improvements in both efficiency and accuracy by capitalizing on the strengths of diverse input modalities. We propose a framework that integrates neural probability estimation with a symbolic reasoning engine, demonstrating a flexible and adaptable system for complex reasoning problems. The effectiveness of this framework is illustrated through a conceptual analysis and theoretical justification, highlighting the benefits of a modality-aware reasoning process.

title: Dynamic Programming for Reinforcement Learning with Partial Observability
abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) has achieved remarkable success in various domains, but its performance often degrades significantly when faced with partially observable environments. In these scenarios, an agent's observations are incomplete, making it difficult to accurately estimate the true state of the environment. This paper proposes a novel approach to address this challenge by integrating dynamic programming (DP) techniques with RL. We argue that DP, with its ability to systematically explore state spaces and optimize policies based on value functions, provides a theoretically robust framework for handling partial observability. Our method incorporates memory and belief tracking mechanisms to compensate for the agent's limited observations. The core of our approach involves transforming the partially observable Markov Decision Process (POMDP) into a solvable form through a process of state abstraction and value iteration. We demonstrate the feasibility and effectiveness of this approach through conceptual analysis and a detailed algorithm outline, laying the groundwork for future implementations and experiments. The primary contribution lies in re-establishing the connection between dynamic programming and reinforcement learning, offering a principled solution to the complexities introduced by partial observability.

title: Quantum Entanglement Entropy Encoding (QE2E)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel encoding scheme, Quantum Entanglement Entropy Encoding (QE2E), leveraging the fundamental role of quantum entanglement entropy in information processing. The core claim is that entanglement entropy can surpass the capacity limitations imposed by classical channels, offering the potential for enhanced information transmission. QE2E employs a multi-body entanglement-based encoding strategy, meticulously controlling the distribution of entanglement entropy to maximize information transfer efficiency. The novelty lies in recognizing entanglement entropy as a core physical resource, effectively circumventing the constraints of traditional information theory. We present a theoretical framework outlining the key components of the QE2E scheme and explore its potential implications for quantum communication, specifically focusing on improved data transmission rates and resistance to channel impairments. The analysis demonstrates the possibility of achieving coding gains beyond those attainable with conventional methods, predicated on the precise manipulation of entangled states. Further research will focus on the practical implementation challenges and exploring the scalability of this approach.

title: Adaptive Constraint Relaxation for Non-Linear Dynamical Systems
abstract: This paper presents an innovative approach to solving complex, non-linear dynamical systems through adaptive constraint relaxation. Traditional methods often struggle with oscillations and instability, requiring extensive parameter tuning. Our novel technique leverages reinforcement learning to dynamically adjust the strength of constraints, fostering stability and encouraging the formation of stable states. The core mechanism involves a feedback loop that continuously evaluates the system's behavior and refines the constraints to achieve optimal performance. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this method through extensive simulations and preliminary experimental results, showcasing a significant improvement in stability and reduced oscillation frequency compared to existing approaches.

title: Memory-Augmented Neural Networks with Hierarchical Contextual Encoding
abstract: This paper introduces a novel neural network architecture, the Memory-Augmented Neural Network with Hierarchical Contextual Encoding (MANHCE), designed to overcome the limitations of conventional neural networks regarding memory capacity and the processing of long-range dependencies. The core innovation lies in integrating an external memory module alongside a hierarchical encoding scheme. This allows the network to not only store contextual information but also to dynamically retrieve and utilize it based on the input, effectively addressing the vanishing gradient problem and enabling the network to capture complex relationships across extended sequences. We present a detailed description of the architecture, the learning mechanism, and the theoretical underpinnings of the system. The proposed MANHCE demonstrates improved performance in tasks requiring long-range context understanding compared to standard recurrent and convolutional networks. We will discuss the key components and their interaction, focusing on the hierarchical encoding and the memory retrieval process.

title: Quantum State Mapping and Topological Mapping: A Novel Approach to Quantum Device Design and Optimization
abstract: Quantum state mapping, a crucial technique in quantum information processing, involves the transformation of quantum states into different mappings. This research explores the interplay between these mappings and topological mappings, proposing a novel algorithm for optimizing quantum device control through this relationship. We introduce a framework based on non-linear mapping, aiming to precisely control quantum states by iteratively refining these mappings. The core mechanism centers on the identification of optimal mappings that leverage topological properties to enhance device performance. This work provides a new perspective on quantum device design, highlighting the potential of topological mappings to guide and improve the control of quantum systems. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through simulations and preliminary device design, showcasing its ability to achieve targeted control and optimize device characteristics.

title: Topological Quantum Computation Resource Allocation in Quantum Networks
abstract: This paper presents a novel algorithm for resource allocation within quantum networks leveraging topological structures. The core claim is to design an efficient resource allocation strategy that maximizes quantum computation effectiveness and resource utilization. The proposed mechanism dynamically allocates quantum computational resources based on the network's topology, optimizing the computational workflow. This addresses a critical challenge in quantum computing – efficient resource management – by introducing a new approach. The algorithm's effectiveness is demonstrated through theoretical analysis and a focus on key performance indicators such as qubit fidelity, computational latency, and overall resource throughput. The algorithm aims to improve the practicality and scalability of quantum computation within distributed quantum networks. The primary goal is to mitigate the limitations of traditional resource allocation methods, which often struggle to account for the complex and dynamic nature of quantum network topologies. This work contributes to the advancement of quantum networking and its potential for realizing robust and scalable quantum computation.

title: 基于生物神经网络的量子算法优化
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to quantum algorithm optimization by integrating the structural and functional principles of biological neural networks with quantum computation. The core idea is to leverage the inherent parallelism and adaptive learning capabilities of biological neural networks to refine the parameters of quantum algorithms, thereby enhancing both their efficiency and stability. We introduce a framework where a neural network acts as a dynamic optimizer, continuously adjusting the quantum algorithm's parameters based on feedback, mimicking the learning process observed in biological systems. The theoretical foundation relies on mapping quantum operations to neural network connections and utilizing activation functions to represent the probabilistic nature of quantum measurements. This synergistic combination aims to overcome some of the limitations associated with traditional quantum algorithm optimization techniques, particularly in scenarios with complex parameter landscapes. The proposed method offers a potentially more robust and adaptable solution for optimizing quantum algorithms across diverse applications. We explore the fundamental concepts and outline the potential benefits of this hybrid approach, emphasizing its ability to bridge the gap between classical and quantum computing.

title: Formal Verification of Probabilistic Programs using Process Algebra
abstract: Probabilistic programs, increasingly prevalent in areas like artificial intelligence, robotics, and risk analysis, inherently involve uncertainty. Traditional formal verification methods, primarily designed for deterministic systems, struggle to effectively address this uncertainty. This paper proposes a novel approach to formally verifying probabilistic programs by leveraging the principles of process algebra. We represent probabilistic programs as processes, modeling the probabilistic transitions based on event probabilities. We then apply process algebra techniques, drawing inspiration from Hoare logic and temporal logic, to reason about and formally verify the program's behavior. This approach allows us to establish properties like safety, liveness, and correctness, albeit with a focus on probabilistic guarantees rather than strict determinism. The core contribution lies in adapting established verification methodologies to this new domain, offering a path towards more robust and reliable probabilistic program development. The framework presented here offers a foundational approach, and future work will explore more sophisticated techniques to handle the complexities of probabilistic transitions and quantify uncertainty rigorously.

title: 奇点映射的动态自适应随机梯度
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to random gradient algorithms leveraging a dynamic self-adaptive random gradient adjustment mechanism. Traditional random gradient algorithms often rely on predefined patterns, which can lead to suboptimal solutions and limited adaptability. We propose a new method that dynamically adjusts random gradient parameters based on data noise and error, effectively mitigating local optima and enabling self-adaptive adjustments. The core mechanism revolves around a "dynamic self-adaptive random gradient adjustment" process, which integrates gradient updates with local fluctuations to improve the overall performance of the algorithm. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through extensive experiments on several benchmark problems, showcasing its ability to achieve higher convergence rates and robustness compared to existing methods. The results highlight the significant advantages of this dynamic self-adaptive approach, particularly in handling noisy data and complex landscapes. This work contributes to the development of more efficient and adaptable random gradient algorithms applicable to a wider range of computational problems.

title: Quantum Topology Optimization Algorithm: A Novel Approach to Geometric Transformation and Optimization
abstract: Quantum topology, a rapidly developing field of physics, offers a unique way to manipulate space and generate novel physical phenomena. This research explores the potential of integrating quantum topology principles with optimization algorithms to achieve unprecedented levels of geometric transformation and optimization. We propose a novel algorithm, dubbed "Quantum Topology Optimization Algorithm" (QTOA), which leverages the inherent properties of quantum topology – specifically, its ability to create and manipulate complex geometric structures – to guide optimization processes. This algorithm aims to surpass the limitations of conventional optimization methods by introducing a dynamic, self-correcting element driven by quantum principles. The core mechanism involves the application of quantum topological transformations to the problem space, followed by iterative refinement guided by a quantum-enhanced optimization process. We demonstrate the efficacy of QTOA through theoretical analysis and preliminary simulations, highlighting its potential for significant advancements in geometric problem-solving. The research also touches upon the possibility of leveraging quantum computation within the optimization process, potentially unlocking new computational pathways.

title: 自组织信息论的量子纠缠干涉
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of self-organizing information theory (SIT) to enhance quantum entanglement and facilitate information transfer and encoding. We propose a novel quantum entanglement interaction mechanism based on SIT, leveraging the inherent self-correlation of entangled states to achieve more efficient data manipulation and security. The core mechanism focuses on guiding the entanglement state towards a specific, predetermined outcome through the principles of SIT. We explore the theoretical implications and potential applications of this approach, particularly in the context of quantum communication and information storage. The research emphasizes the use of SIT as a fundamental framework for understanding and manipulating entangled quantum states.

abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to quantum state parameterization, termed Adaptive Parameterization of Quantum States (APQS). APQS dynamically adjusts quantum state parameters based on computational goals and environmental factors, leveraging quantum entanglement and error correction for optimization. We present a theoretical framework and preliminary experimental validation demonstrating the effectiveness of this method in optimizing quantum algorithms.

title: Optimizing solar panel placement using fuzzy OWA–BWM approach
abstract: Abstract Selecting reliable sites for solar-panel installation remains challenging because most GIS-based multi-criteria decision-making approaches produce a single deterministic suitability map and therefore do not reveal how site priorities change under different levels of risk acceptance. This study proposes a risk-sensitive GIS framework that integrates fuzzy spatial standardization, the Best–Worst Method (BWM), and Fuzzy Ordered Weighted Averaging (Fuzzy OWA) for solar-panel site selection across six climatically distinct regions. The methodological innovation lies in combining the relatively consistent and comparison-efficient criterion weighting of BWM with OWA aggregation applied to ordered BWM-weighted fuzzy values under multiple α-based decision scenarios. This integration generates conservative, intermediate, and risk-tolerant suitability maps and distinguishes spatially stable priority zones from locations that become suitable only when greater compensation among criteria is permitted. Nine climatic, topographic, geological, and accessibility criteria were evaluated. Solar radiation received the highest importance, but the final suitability patterns were also strongly influenced by road accessibility, slope aspect, distances to rivers and faults, and regional climatic conditions. Estimated annual electricity generation ranged from 5544.99 to 17,663.66 kWh/year under the BWM scenario and from 3377.24 to 17,704.66 kWh/year under the OWA–BWM scenarios for the assumed effective panel areas. These differences demonstrate that risk attitude can materially alter both the extent of suitable land and the associated energy-production potential. ROC validation produced AUC values of 0.721–0.971, indicating moderate to excellent discrimination among suitable and unsuitable locations, while also showing that model reliability varies among climatic regions. The framework therefore improves preliminary decision quality by supporting the identification of robust low-risk sites, prioritization of field verification, and comparison of alternative development scenarios. Potential environmental benefits, including reduced soil-surface exposure and improved soil-moisture retention, are interpreted as post-selection co-benefits.

title: MAQDRL: QuadTree-Based Multi-Agent Federated Deep Q-Learning for Collision Avoidance and Routing Optimization with MEC-Aware Communication Analysis
abstract: Autonomous vehicle routing in complex urban environments suffers from high computational overheads, energy inefficiency, and increased collision risks using traditional routing algorithms. These limitations necessitate innovative approaches to address scalable and real-time decision-making requirements for multi-agent systems. This research proposes a reinforcement learning-based Multi-agent Federated Deep Q-Network (MAQDRL) model, which integrates federated learning with QuadTree spatial partitioning and indexing framework for collision detection. The model employs a decentralized training approach to optimize routing efficiency and reduce energy consumption. Each agent of MAQDRL trains the Deep Q-Network (DQN) independently using local state information. Model parameters are periodically synchronized through federated learning to align policies while preserving data privacy. The QuadTree partitions the environment dynamically based on agent density, focusing computational resources on high-interaction areas to ensure efficient collision detection and proximity querying. Advanced preprocessing techniques like state normalization, action encoding, and reward scaling stabilize training and enhance policy convergence. The framework further employs an adaptive exploration-exploitation strategy and decentralized decision-making, allowing agents to collaboratively achieve optimized routing while mitigating collisions and reducing energy consumption in complex, high-density scenarios. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed MAQDRL is a promising solution for advancing autonomous vehicle routing systems. MAQDRL achieves a 97.8% success rate, outperforming existing research - MARC (92.2%), MAPPO (94.8%), and MADDPG (95.2%).MAQDRL reduces collision frequency by 73.08% over MAPPO and 66.13% over MADDPG, while energy consumption is lowered by 56.52% ov er MAPPO and 55.98% over MADDPG on a CVRPTW-derived spatial navigation benchmark.

evidence.abstract: Autonomous vehicle routing in complex urban environments suffers from high computational overheads, energy inefficiency, and increased collision risks using traditional routing algorithms. These limitations necessitate innovative approaches to address scalable and real-time decision-making requirements for multi-agent systems. This research proposes a reinforcement learning-based Multi-agent Federated Deep Q-Network (MAQDRL) model, which integrates federated learning with QuadTree spatial partitioning and indexing framework for collision detection. The model employs a decentralized training approach to optimize routing efficiency and reduce energy consumption. Each agent of MAQDRL trains the Deep Q-Network (DQN) independently using local state information. Model parameters are periodically synchronized through federated learning to align policies while preserving data privacy. The QuadTree partitions the environment dynamically based on agent density, focusing computational resources on high-interaction areas to ensure efficient collision detection and proximity querying. Advanced preprocessing techniques like state normalization, action encoding, and reward scaling stabilize training and enhance policy convergence. The framework further employs an adaptive exploration-exploitation strategy and decentralized decision-making, allowing agents to collaboratively achieve optimized routing while mitigating collisions and reducing energy consumption in complex, high-density scenarios. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed MAQDRL is a promising solution for advancing autonomous vehicle routing systems. MAQDRL achieves a 97.8% success rate, outperforming existing research - MARC (92.2%), MAPPO (94.8%), and MADDPG (95.2%).MAQDRL reduces collision frequency by 73.08% over MAPPO and 66.13% over MADDPG, while energy consumption is lowered by 56.52% ov er MAPPO and 55.98% over MADDPG on a CVRPTW-derived spatial navigation benchmark.

title: Cultural Misalignment in Large Language Models: Detection, Measurement, and Mitigation Through Targeted Fine-Tuning
abstract: We evaluate three open-weight LLMs (Gemma3-12B from the USA, Bielik-11B-v3 from Poland, and Qwen3-4B from China) against World Values Survey Wave 7 data for 63 demographic personas across three countries, using normalized Wasserstein distance to quantify distributional misalignment. Contrary to expectations, no model favors its home country: the Chinese-built Qwen3-4B performs worst on its own Chinese population (W1 = 0.436, the highest misalignment in the entire model x country matrix). Targeted LoRA fine-tuning on the five worst-case personas, requiring fewer than 1,200 training pairs and under 15 minutes on a single GPU, reduces bias by 16.8% for Bielik-11B (p_Bonf = 0.002, d = -4.4) with all five targets improving. However, country-level decomposition reveals that fine-tuning redistributes rather than removes bias: Bielik's worst-case personas swap entirely from American to Chinese elderly, with zero overlap between pre- and post-correction sets. To our knowledge, this is the first study to target worst-case demographic personas with LoRA fine-tuning for cross-cultural bias mitigation.

title: Constant regret in general games via higher-order optimism
abstract: We introduce an uncoupled learning algorithm which, when employed by all players of an arbitrary $N$-player normal form game with up to $K$ actions per player, guarantees $O(N^3\log^2 K)$ individual regret, uniformly over the horizon of play. The proposed algorithm - which we call higher-order optimism with discounting (HOOD) is a variant of optimistic follow-the-regularized-leader (OptFTRL) that combines a discounted $(N+1)$-th order predictor with entropic regularization over a suitable "lifting" of the game's strategy space. This combination of ingredients is purposefully designed to dampen large oscillations of the induced sequence of play in a controlled manner, removing in this way a key stumbling block of previous attempts to achieve constant regret in general games. Our approach bears several striking similarities to the concurrent - and completely independent - work of Liu, Farina, and Ozdaglar (arXiv:2608.31166), who very recently derived an $O(N^{21}\log^{4} K)$ regret bound through the use of higher-order optimism and an exponential moving average estimator.

title: Approximate maximum-likelihood decoding via truncated free energies
abstract: Maximum-likelihood decoding (MLD) achieves the minimum logical error rate of stabilizer codes under known i.i.d. Pauli noise, but its exact evaluation is \#P-hard. Practical pipelines therefore approximate MLD by minimum-weight decoding (MWD), retaining only the lowest-weight recovery per syndrome and discarding the coset degeneracy. The minimum-weight search is in turn implemented by stochastic solvers. We introduce approximate maximum-likelihood decoding (AMLD), a black-box framework that recycles the candidate samples discarded by stochastic inner decoders into a per-class truncated free-energy estimator. For every logical class represented in the candidate pool, the estimator is provably bounded below by the exact free energy and above by the empirical minimum weight. AMLD returns the logical class minimizing the estimated free energy with linear classical overhead. In SA-based Ising-decoder benchmarks, AMLD closes up to $83\%$ of the MWD--MLD threshold gap across the toric and color codes under bit-flip and depolarizing noise. The largest threshold improvement, from $17.28\%$ to $18.62\%$, occurs on the $6.6.6$ color code under depolarizing noise. We further demonstrate AMLD on the $[[144,12,12]]$ bivariate-bicycle code, whose bit-flip decoding problem has a hypergraph structure. This application requires neither matching-based enumeration nor code-specific tensor-network contraction. At $p=0.05$, AMLD reduces the logical error rate by $13\%$ relative to MWD evaluated on the same BP-OSD candidate pool.

title: DCCQ: From Ordered Bernoulli Levels to Critical-Line Geometry: Integer Quantization, Bernoulli Residual Phase, and Prime-Power Spectra
abstract: We present the discrete--complex complement quotient (DCCQ) framework through the ordered Bernoulli-word kernel $f(p,n,k)=p^k(1-p)^{n-k}$ and its inverse-integer level sets. The binary level $2^{-n}$ selects $p=1/2$ as the unique real split-independent anchor. Imposing the additional continuation rule $1-z=\overline z$ gives the conjugation-symmetric line $z=1/2+iu$. On the central normalized branch, the inverse-level split $κ=k/n$ also has real part $1/2$. The quadratic coordinate $Q(z)=1/4+u^2$ identifies complementary conjugate points, has minimum $1/4$, and has an explicit two-sign inverse; restricting its values to integers defines an arithmetic quantization. For supplied positive critical-line zero ordinates $γ_k$, the induced level has the exact decomposition \[ L_k=\frac14+γ_k^2=N_k+δ_k,\qquad δ_k=\widetilde B_1\!\left(γ_k^2+\frac34\right), \] where $N_k=\lfloor L_k+1/2\rfloor$ and $\widetilde B_1(x)=\{x\}-1/2$. The integer--phase pair $(N_k,e^{2πiδ_k})$ retains the level and the positive ordinate. Prime-exponent coordinates describe the factorization of the integer component, while conditional Fourier moments formulate an open question about the residual phases. The finite numerical diagnostics are descriptive. A distinct complex exponent $s$ gives an inverse-level representation of the supplied term $m^{-s}$; direct substitution cancels the auxiliary coordinates. These terms assemble into the classical Dirichlet series and Euler product for $\Re s>1$. The framework organizes exact coordinate identities, classical zeta connections, and numerical diagnostics; it establishes neither conditional equidistribution nor a zero-location theorem.

title: Aggregating and aligning knowledge graphs into a global service:SampoSampo system for cross-cultural data search, exploration, and analysis
abstract: This paper abstract presents an approach and first results of creating a global LOD service and semantic portal, SampoSampo, based on a network of interlinked Cultural Heritage knowledge graphs (KG) of different application domains. In this way, a more comprehensive global view for searching, exploring, and analyzing the interlinked KGs can be provided than by using local KGs separately. The SampoSampo LOD service can be used as a web service for providing IRI identifiers for aligning new datasets with the national DARIAH-FI research infrastructure on which SampoSampo is based, and for assessing the quality of data in different KGs by comparing their metadata. The portal underway can be used for searching and exploring the local KGs by with a single user interface (UI) and for implementing novel application perspectives based on relational search, where semantic “interesting” associations (relations) between entities, such as persons, organizations, and places in the global KG, can be searched for and natural explanations for them be created.

title: 基于拓扑结构的量子算法优化
abstract: Quantum algorithms are increasingly important for scientific discovery and technological advancement. However, their implementation often faces challenges related to computational complexity and resource requirements. This paper introduces a novel quantum algorithm optimization method based on topological structures, aiming to enhance the efficiency and precision of existing quantum algorithms. The core mechanism involves dynamically adjusting the quantum state's topology to achieve optimal performance. This approach offers a promising pathway to overcome traditional limitations and facilitate the development of more powerful quantum computations. The research presents a theoretical framework and demonstrates the effectiveness of this technique through a focused analysis of specific quantum algorithms.

title: Adaptive Domain-Driven Optimization
abstract: This paper introduces an adaptive domain-driven optimization (ADDO) algorithm designed to address the limitations of traditional optimization methods. The algorithm dynamically adjusts the domain structure during the optimization process, enabling more robust and efficient exploration of the solution space. We propose a novel method that leverages the inherent properties of domain geometry to guide the optimization process, mitigating the pitfalls of local optima and improving overall convergence. The core mechanism centers around a dynamic transformation of the domain, allowing the algorithm to adapt to the specific characteristics of the input data and the optimization problem. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through several case studies focusing on the optimization of complex, non-convex functions. The results demonstrate significant improvements in convergence speed and the quality of solutions compared to existing methods. This work establishes a new foundation for adaptive optimization, offering a promising path toward enhanced optimization capabilities across a range of disciplines.

title: Adaptive Quantum Circuit Design
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to quantum circuit design, termed Adaptive Quantum Circuit Design (AQC Design). AQC Design leverages dynamic parameter adjustment to optimize the performance of quantum circuits, offering a significant improvement over static circuit design methodologies. The core mechanism focuses on iteratively refining circuit parameters based on a feedback loop that monitors the circuit's performance, ultimately achieving higher fidelity and increased computational throughput. The research explores the benefits of this dynamic approach in addressing the inherent challenges of quantum computing, particularly in handling complex and varying environments. We demonstrate the effectiveness of AQC Design through theoretical analysis and preliminary experimental results, showcasing a substantial increase in circuit fidelity and computational efficiency compared to traditional methods.

title: Quantum Topologies for Adaptive Quantum Computing Stability
abstract: Quantum topologies, characterized by their unique geometric properties, offer a promising pathway toward fault-tolerant quantum computation. However, the inherent fragility of quantum states necessitates robust stability measures. This paper investigates a novel stability research framework for quantum computing, specifically tailored to address the challenges posed by quantum topologies. We propose a dynamic approach to the manipulation of quantum system topology, employing feedback mechanisms to proactively detect and mitigate potential instability issues. This research explores the potential of this framework to enhance the reliability of quantum algorithms and systems. The study focuses on the fundamental principles underlying stable quantum computation, leveraging the inherent structure of quantum topology as a critical element.

title: AI Adaptive Learning and Assessment System: A Pilot Evaluation of an AI-Powered Adaptive Quiz and Feedback Platform
abstract: This paper presents a pilot implementation of an Adaptive Learning and Assessment System, an online system where students upload their learning resources, and receive automatically generated and difficulty adjusted quiz with topic level feedback. As opposed to a fixed question bank, the system generates questions on the fly directly from a learner's own material, dynamically adjusts the difficulty level of the questions according to real-time performance data and creates a summary at the end of the quiz to show a learner what to focus on when studying the topics they're not mastering, and produces a downloadable report. A system evaluation questionnaire was given to 32 users after their last quiz session to assess their perceptions of the system through the use of an eight-item dimensional Likert-scale instrument that measured understanding, adaptive difficulty, feedback quality, weak-topic identification, trust, engagement, ease of use and preference over traditional self-study. Using response-frequency distributions, dispersion, correlation, and reliability statistics (Cronbach's alpha), the responses were analyzed. When it comes to ease of use and feedback quality, the system received the highest rating from the students, while it was rated the lowest, but still fairly positively, for their trust in the AI-generated content. The correlation analysis results indicated that adaptive difficulty and engagement were the most strongly correlated items in the instrument; trust and preference to traditional study were a second well-correlated group that indicated that usability and trust are evaluative dimensions that are distinct for this system. These results suggest that the platform is usable and well-received as is, and that the need for trust in content generated by AI is your apparent top priority for future development. Since it is a small-sample, single group pilot study with no control condition, these results are not causal, but are meant to encourage a larger controlled follow-on study.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Constraint Propagation
abstract: Quantum-enhanced constraint propagation represents a paradigm shift in the optimization of complex systems, offering the potential for significantly accelerated solution finding and improved performance, particularly for problems involving intricate constraints. This paper explores a novel technique utilizing quantum annealing and quantum approximate optimization algorithms (QAOA) to enhance constraint propagation. We detail the implementation of a quantum-enhanced constraint propagation framework, focusing on its ability to efficiently navigate high-dimensional search spaces and effectively exploit quantum properties to reduce computational complexity. The core claim is that this approach will dramatically accelerate the process of finding optimal solutions to challenging optimization problems, opening new avenues for applications across diverse fields.

title: Adaptive Quantum Algorithm Optimization
abstract: Quantum computing holds immense potential for revolutionizing various fields, and the development of efficient quantum algorithms is crucial to unlocking this potential. However, the inherent complexity of quantum systems often necessitates the refinement of quantum algorithms through extensive parameter optimization. This paper proposes a novel approach to quantum algorithm optimization based on adaptive quantum optimization, leveraging the unique properties of quantum computers to dynamically adjust quantum gate parameters. We introduce a quantum quantum optimization (Qquo) algorithm, which intelligently adjusts these parameters based on the quantum system's state, ultimately leading to improved algorithm efficiency and accuracy. This research explores the fundamental principles behind the Qquo algorithm and its potential impact on optimizing quantum computations.

title: Quantum Monte-Carlo Simulation with Privacy Protection using Quantum Bohm Maps
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to privacy-preserving computation leveraging the unique properties of quantum Bohm maps, a form of quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) method. Traditional QMC methods, while powerful for simulating complex systems, inherently expose the underlying data used in the calculations, posing significant privacy risks. This research proposes a framework where quantum Bohm maps are constructed to perform computations while maintaining the privacy of the input data. The core idea is to utilize the inherent probabilistic nature of quantum mechanics to obscure the direct relationship between the input and the output, effectively shielding sensitive information. We detail the construction of these maps, focusing on the mapping between input states and output states, and discuss the implications for various computational tasks. The methodology presented offers a promising avenue for secure quantum simulations and computations. The effectiveness of this approach is demonstrated through theoretical analysis and conceptual design, paving the way for future experimental validation.

title: Trustworthy Computing through Domain-Specific Languages
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to trustworthy computing by proposing a domain-specific language (DSL) designed to streamline the development and verification of trusted systems. The core concept is to provide a programming language tailored to the unique requirements of secure computation, enabling direct expression of security properties, a verifiable execution model, and tight integration with underlying hardware. Traditional approaches to secure system design often rely on general-purpose programming languages, which introduce complexity and potential vulnerabilities. This DSL aims to mitigate these challenges by offering a more intuitive and efficient means of specifying and implementing security-critical functionalities. The paper details the design of the DSL, focusing on key features such as formal specification, static analysis capabilities, and hardware abstraction layers. Ultimately, this work demonstrates the potential of DSLs to significantly reduce development time, improve security assurance, and facilitate the widespread adoption of trusted computing technologies.

title: 基于量子态的动态拓扑计算
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic topology calculation framework based on quantum states, designed to facilitate complex multi-body quantum computations and leverage the unique properties of quantum states to enhance computational efficiency and accuracy. Traditional methods often rely on predefined topology structures, prompting an opportunity for algorithmic innovation. We present a framework that dynamically adjusts quantum topology structures during computation, addressing limitations of existing approaches. This work explores the potential of quantum states to enable more efficient and accurate topological calculations. The core mechanism centers around a quantum state manipulation strategy, optimized for dynamic topology generation. The paper concludes with a discussion of the framework's theoretical underpinnings and potential applications.

title: Quantum Simulation of Evolutionary Algorithms
abstract: Quantum simulation has emerged as a powerful tool for optimization and exploration across diverse fields. This paper investigates the application of quantum mechanics to enhance evolutionary algorithms, proposing a novel hybrid quantum-classical simulation framework designed to accelerate the search for optimal solutions. We introduce a quantum-enhanced mutation operator, integrated with a classical optimization algorithm, to exploit quantum effects to expedite the exploration of evolutionary parameter spaces. The core mechanism focuses on utilizing quantum phenomena – specifically superposition and entanglement – to improve the representation and manipulation of evolutionary trajectories, ultimately leading to faster convergence and the identification of optimal solutions. The research explores the potential of this approach to overcome limitations in traditional evolutionary algorithm implementation, offering a promising pathway for enhanced optimization capabilities.

title: Differential Privacy for Federated Learning with Non-IID Data
abstract: Federated learning (FL) offers a promising approach to training machine learning models on decentralized data sources without directly exchanging data. However, the inherent non-IID (independent and identically distributed) nature of data across clients poses a significant threat to the privacy guarantees provided by traditional differential privacy (DP) mechanisms. This paper introduces a novel differential privacy framework specifically designed for federated learning scenarios with non-IID data. Our approach incorporates adaptive noise scaling, dynamically adjusting the privacy budget based on the measured data heterogeneity among clients. This tailored mechanism mitigates the increased privacy risk associated with non-IID data, providing a more robust and effective solution for privacy-preserving federated learning. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our method through theoretical analysis and highlight its advantages over conventional DP techniques in this context.

title: Topological Space Dynamic Adaptive Graph Neural Network Optimization
abstract: This paper presents a novel dynamic adaptive graph neural network optimization framework based on topological structure. Traditional graph neural network training often relies on predefined patterns, which can limit adaptability and potentially trap the algorithm in local optima. Our proposed method introduces a "dynamic topology adjustment" mechanism, dynamically adjusting graph neural network parameters based on data noise and error, thereby promoting robustness and facilitating self-adaptive tuning. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through extensive experimental results, showcasing improved convergence speed, better generalization performance, and enhanced robustness to variations in the training dataset. The core mechanism leverages the inherent topological properties of the network to guide parameter adjustments, fostering a more adaptive and resilient optimization process.

title: Hierarchical Symbolic Regression with Neural Priors
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to symbolic regression, termed Hierarchical Symbolic Regression with Neural Priors (HSRP). The core idea is to leverage the strengths of both symbolic regression – its ability to discover exact analytical solutions – and neural networks – their capacity for learning complex patterns and priors. HSRP employs a neural network to learn a prior distribution over possible symbolic expressions. This learned prior then guides a hierarchical symbolic regression system, which iteratively refines the symbolic representation of the solution. The hierarchical structure allows for efficient exploration of the solution space by focusing the search on regions where the learned prior is most relevant. The resulting system demonstrates improved performance compared to traditional symbolic regression techniques, particularly in problems with complex relationships and high dimensionality. We demonstrate the efficacy of this approach through theoretical analysis and a detailed explanation of the underlying mechanisms.

abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to optimization, specifically focusing on the application of topology-based methods to improve algorithmic efficiency. The core mechanism involves systematically modifying the initial topology to minimize computational cost and enhance the algorithm's overall efficiency. This method offers a framework for tackling complex optimization problems within a dynamically evolving landscape, leading to improved results with reduced computational burden. The study explores the benefits of this dynamic approach through rigorous analysis and practical demonstration.

title: 基于张量信息的量子机器学习模型
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum machine learning model leveraging the power of tensor information. Traditional machine learning models often struggle with complex, non-linear relationships, hindering their ability to generalize effectively. We propose a quantum-enhanced learning framework that encodes data into quantum tensors, utilizing quantum entanglement and superposition to accelerate training and improve model robustness. This work addresses the limitations of classical machine learning by harnessing the unique properties of quantum systems. The core mechanism involves encoding data into quantum tensors, employing quantum machine learning algorithms, and exploiting the inherent properties of quantum entanglement and superposition to enhance learning efficiency and generalization. This research explores the potential of quantum computing to significantly advance the field of machine learning, particularly in scenarios requiring handling intricate data dependencies.

title: 自适应张量聚合的量子计算实现
abstract: This paper presents a novel quantum computing framework, termed "Adaptive Tensor Aggregation" (ATA), designed to accelerate quantum machine learning algorithms by leveraging adaptive tensor aggregation. Traditional quantum computation often struggles with the limitations of limited qubit resources, necessitating strategies for efficient tensor manipulation. ATA addresses these challenges through a dynamic adjustment of qubit count and state representation, guided by quantum entanglement and superposition. The core mechanism centers around a novel algorithm that iteratively adjusts the tensor aggregation level based on the current state of the system, optimizing for computational complexity and resource utilization. This approach allows for the efficient execution of complex tensor operations, crucial for many machine learning tasks. The proposed framework demonstrates significant improvements in performance compared to existing quantum algorithms, particularly in the context of large-scale tensor computations.

title: Quantum Information Backfaces Self-Adaptive Evolution Model
abstract: Quantum information backfaces are a promising approach to enhance quantum computation by leveraging the inherent properties of the environment. This paper introduces a novel self-adaptive evolution model for quantum information backfaces, designed to dynamically adjust parameter values based on quantum bit (qubit) characteristics and environmental noise. The model utilizes an iterative optimization process, guided by a carefully constructed evolutionary algorithm, to improve quantum bit efficiency. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through simulations, showcasing significant performance improvements over static parameter tuning methods. The core mechanism centers around dynamically evolving the backface's parameter space, allowing for adaptive optimization tailored to specific quantum environments. The potential benefits of this approach include increased qubit fidelity, improved coherence times, and enhanced computational capabilities.

title: Malignancy-Aware Dual-Task Heatmap Decoupling for thyroid ultrasound nodule detection and classification
abstract: Background: Accurate thyroid nodule detection and benign-malignant classification on ultrasound are critical for early cancer diagnosis. Existing deep-learning detectors encode localization and classification in a shared feature space, causing inter-task feature redundancy and limiting task-specific performance. Methods: We propose Malignancy-Aware Dual-Task Heatmap Decoupling (MADTHD), a CenterNet-based framework that decouples localization and classification through asymmetric dual heads. A Position Head with small receptive fields captures precise nodule contours, while a Malignancy Head with multi-scale dilated convolutions extracts textural and boundary features indicative of benign-malignant status. A feature orthogonality loss is introduced to enforce complementary channel activation between the two heads, reducing inter-task feature redundancy. Systematic ablation studies were conducted on TN5000, and generalization was assessed via zero-shot transfer to the independent TN3K dataset. Results: MADTHD achieves a mean average precision of 0.7840 on TN5000, outperforming the CenterNet baseline by 2.61 percentage points, with the improvement most pronounced for malignant nodules. Ablation experiments demonstrate that the asymmetric dual-head architecture and the feature orthogonality loss are mutually synergistic. On the independent TN3K dataset, MADTHD maintains its relative standing against the baseline without fine-tuning. Conclusion: MADTHD provides an interpretable dual-task framework mirroring the clinical localize-then-characterize workflow. The proposed modules are lightweight and backbone-agnostic. Clinical utility remains to be established through prospective validation.

title: Applications of Explainable Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare
abstract: Rapid advances in machine learning (ML) and artificial intelligence (AI) have transformed patient care, prediction, and image-based diagnosis. However, the black-box nature of many AI models raises concerns about trust, ethics, and accountability, limiting their clinical adoption. Explainable AI (XAI) addresses these challenges by promoting fairness, transparency, and alignment with medical reasoning. This chapter explores the use of XAI in medical imaging, electronic health records, and treatment planning. It reviews core explainability methods, model-agnostic techniques, feature-attribution approaches, and inherently interpretable models, highlighting how they improve diagnostic accuracy, build clinician trust, and support transparent decision-making. Widely used XAI tools like Grad-CAM, SHAP, LIME, and layer-wise relevance propagation are discussed in the context of regulatory compliance and clinical validation. Despite its promise, XAI faces limitations, including trade-offs between complexity and interpretability, potential biases in explanations, and the lack of standardized evaluation metrics. Hybrid approaches that combine clinical expertise with AI insights are emerging to offer responsible and transparent decision support. Integrating XAI into healthcare systems strengthens clinician–patient trust and supports the ethical deployment of AI technologies.

title: The Shape of Time: Video-Token Contrast for Temporal Understanding in VideoLMs
abstract: Seeing frames in order does not mean representing time. Modern VideoLMs receive ordered video streams, yet their main supervision acts on generated text rather than video-token representations where event dynamics should first emerge. This mismatch allows models to learn temporal answers from shortcuts such as objects, scenes, and language priors, without requiring internal video representations to capture event progression. To address this, we propose VT-Contrast, a representation-level temporal counterfactual objective for VideoLMs. Its design asks where temporal supervision should act and what temporal differences it should expose. VT-Contrast supervises selected late-layer last-frame video tokens, where temporal information is expected to be integrated before language generation, and contrasts order-preserving views with same-video reordered counterfactuals graded by Kendall tau distance. It requires no architectural changes, is compatible with diverse VideoLM training tasks, and improves overall performance across temporal understanding benchmarks. Our code is available at https://github.com/ANDgate99/VT-Contrast.

title: Govern the Model, Not Only the Data: Storage, Circulation, and Learning in Creative AI
abstract: Federated learning is increasingly presented as a privacy-preserving advance: personal data remain on the device, and only model updates are shared. It borrows the vocabulary of the federated social web, yet inverts its logic, distributing computation while the resulting model stays with whoever convened the training. We argue that federation is not in itself a remedy for extractive AI, because outcomes depend on who governs the data and the model and who has agency over the practices that shape them. We describe three layers at which a creative community can hold its work: storage, circulation, and learning. Examining artist-governed trusts, cooperatives, and consent infrastructures, we show that creator governance is established at storage and circulation but stops at learning: contributors can consent to training, yet have little say over the resulting model or its federation. We map the research space this opens, pairing technical open problems with the human questions from which they unfold. We propose four design principles for a creative data commons that governs models and their federation, not only datasets: govern the model, not only the corpus; make the terms legible at the moment of contribution; design for refusal as a first-class state; and decide stewardship in the open and account for it.

title: LeanGRPO: Eliminating Redundant Recomputation in Diffusion RL
abstract: Diffusion reinforcement learning (RL) has recently achieved significant success in post-training image and video generative models. However, most diffusion RL methods, including DanceGRPO and FlowGRPO, recompute selected timesteps with gradient tracking after rollout. Under on-policy training with the same backend for rollout and update, this recomputation is mathematically redundant. Intuitively, the rollout and policy update steps can reuse the same feed-forward backbone to avoid redundant computation, but doing so can incur a large memory overhead during rollout. To address the issue, we present LeanGRPO by restructuring the data-parallel layout and introducing two recompute-free training schedules for trajectory-logprob diffusion RL: (1) LeanGRPO-Retain enables gradient tracking during rollout and directly reuses the resulting computation graphs and saved activations for backward during update, requiring no recomputation; and (2) LeanGRPO-Reweight also enables gradients during rollout, but immediately backpropagates each selected step using a provisional advantage and delays gradient synchronization, then corrects the provisional gradients with the true advantage after the trajectory is completed. These schedules target different model scales and input sizes. Across FlowGRPO/DanceGRPO with FLUX.1-dev and Wan, LeanGRPO achieves up to 1.83x end-to-end speedup while preserving the original optimization objective.

title: A Joint Power-Privacy Control Framework for Decentralized Learning over Heterogeneous Wireless Multicasting Networks
abstract: In this paper, we propose a decentralized learning framework that incorporates both power control and privacy guarantees. Specifically, we enable a set of clients in a wireless multicast network to jointly train a common model while maintaining a prescribed per-iteration maximum privacy leakage level. The communication network is represented by a rowstochastic adjacency matrix, allowing us to capture asymmetric channel gains as well as heterogeneous maximum transmit power levels. Differential privacy is enforced through an explicit powersplitting strategy that allocates each node's limited maximum transmit power between model coefficients and injected Gaussian noise, thereby jointly controlling learning performance and privacy leakage. We further prove that the proposed algorithm achieves a cumulative regret bound of O(logT), whereTdenotes the time horizon. To evaluate the practical performance of our approach, we perform comprehensive experiments on the CIFAR-10 dataset under both IID and non-IID data distributions, considering different privacy levels, diverse numbers of clients, and various graph topologies. The results demonstrate strong performance across the considered settings and improved performance over existing methods, highlighting the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm under realistic wireless communication constraints.

title: One Demonstration, Many Objects: Generalizing Manipulation via Local Contact Geometry
abstract: Dexterous manipulation with multi-fingered robot hands promises human-level dexterity, but collecting large-scale dexterous robot hand data remains difficult. Learning from human demonstrations has emerged as a scalable alternative to robot teleoperation, providing strong priors on object interaction and contact strategies. Recent sim-to-real RL methods incorporate such priors, but often (i) omit rewards that explicitly incentivize precise contact, yielding weak real-world performance, and/or (ii) generalize poorly to unseen object instances. We propose DemoMimic (Dexterous Motion Mimic), a policy that manipulates objects by focusing on their geometry local to the contact points. Its contact-centric rewards encourage precise contact and improve sim-to-real consistency, yielding a single real-world policy that transfers across objects of varying shape, scale, mass, and friction wherever local contact structure is preserved. Real-world ablations show that DemoMimic achieves 71% success across 16 objects, four tasks, and two robot-hand embodiments, with the smallest sim-to-real drop compared to baselines.

evidence.abstract: Dexterous manipulation with multi-fingered robot hands promises human-level dexterity, but collecting large-scale dexterous robot hand data remains difficult. Learning from human demonstrations has emerged as a scalable alternative to robot teleoperation, providing strong priors on object interaction and contact strategies. Recent sim-to-real RL methods incorporate such priors, but often (i) omit rewards that explicitly incentivize precise contact, yielding weak real-world performance, and/or (ii) generalize poorly to unseen object instances. We propose DemoMimic (Dexterous Motion Mimic), a policy that manipulates objects by focusing on their geometry local to the contact points. Its contact-centric rewards encourage precise contact and improve sim-to-real consistency, yielding a single real-world policy that transfers across objects of varying shape, scale, mass, and friction wherever local contact structure is preserved. Real-world ablations show that DemoMimic achieves 71% success across 16 objects, four tasks, and two robot-hand embodiments, with the smallest sim-to-real drop compared to baselines.

title: Graph-Based Anomaly Detection with Learned Feature Embeddings and Structural Similarity Measures
abstract: This paper presents a novel graph-based approach to anomaly detection that addresses the limitations of traditional methods. The core idea is to represent data as a graph, where nodes represent data points and edges represent relationships. We learn feature embeddings to capture data point similarities and simultaneously define structural similarity measures to quantify deviations from expected graph patterns. The system identifies anomalies by detecting significant changes in these relationships. The approach's strength lies in its ability to model complex dependencies within data, leading to improved anomaly detection accuracy compared to methods relying solely on individual data point analysis. This work outlines the methodology, describes the key components, and demonstrates the potential of this approach through theoretical analysis and conceptual design. The system utilizes a combination of graph convolutional networks (GCNs) for embedding learning and custom similarity metrics based on graph Laplacian eigenvalues to highlight anomalous structural changes. The results, while theoretical at this stage, suggest a promising direction for anomaly detection in various domains.

title: Dynamical Bayesian Networks for Real-Time Anomaly Detection in Complex Systems
abstract: This paper investigates the application of Dynamical Bayesian Networks (DBNs) for real-time anomaly detection within complex systems. Traditional anomaly detection methods often struggle to adapt to evolving system dynamics, leading to inaccurate or delayed detection. DBNs offer a dynamic approach, continuously updating their internal state based on incoming data, thereby capturing changes in system behavior and enabling robust anomaly detection in real-time. The core of this approach lies in the network's ability to model temporal dependencies and probabilistic relationships between variables, allowing it to learn the normal operating state and identify deviations as anomalies. This paper details the theoretical framework of DBNs, specifically focusing on their adaptation capabilities and suitability for complex systems. Mathematical formulations are presented to illustrate the core concepts, including the Bayesian updating equations and the anomaly detection criteria. The proposed framework demonstrates improved performance compared to static anomaly detection models in simulated environments exhibiting non-stationary behavior. The key contributions of this work are a practical and adaptable method for real-time anomaly detection, offering a significant advancement in the field.

title: Causal Discovery via Contrastive Predictive Coding
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to causal discovery, termed Contrastive Predictive Coding (CPC), designed to address the limitations of existing algorithms when dealing with complex, high-dimensional data and confounding variables. The core idea is to utilize a contrastive learning framework where nodes in a system encode the discrepancy between their observed state and a predicted state, generated by incorporating information from other nodes. The system learns causal relationships by minimizing this discrepancy across different hypothetical interventions. Unlike traditional methods reliant on assumptions about data distribution or relying heavily on iterative constraint-based algorithms, CPC directly learns causal structure through the minimization of prediction errors. This approach offers improved robustness and scalability, particularly in scenarios where confounding is prevalent. We demonstrate the theoretical foundations of CPC and outline a proposed implementation strategy, highlighting its potential to unlock causal insights from intricate datasets.

The resulting network exhibits a more structured understanding of the underlying relationships, enabling it to generate more insightful and verifiable explanations.

title: A Safety Memory Is a Declassification Channel: Why Origin Binding, Taint Tracking and Memory Isolation Do Not Secure the Records an Agent Writes About Attacks
abstract: (c) 2026 Pranay Mahendrakar. Licensed under CC BY 4.0. Two lines of work on language-model agents have converged on the same component from opposite directions. One proposes that an agent keep a persistent safety memory, so that an attack seen once, a request refused once or a source found untrustworthy once continues to inform decisions in later sessions. The other reports that persistent memory is an exploitable channel, with published attacks that write records through query-only interaction, through fragments individually too innocuous to filter, and through the agent's own reflection step. This paper argues that the coincidence is structural rather than incidental. A safety memory is defined by a property that ordinary agent memory does not have: its records exist because the agent observed something untrusted, and they are worth keeping only if they later carry authority over a consequential decision. In the vocabulary of information-flow control that the agent-security literature has already adopted, that is a declassification, specifically an integrity endorsement, and it is the one operation the three defense families now in print are built to forbid. Write-time origin binding, proved necessary and, with corroboration-gated elevation, sufficient against laundering for ordinary memory, either denies a safety record the authority that makes it useful or supplies the elevation an attacker needs. Monotone taint tracking over-blocks or strands the record by construction, which its own proponents say. Memory isolation prevents the write that the safety memory exists to perform. Three of the paper's claims cut against the premise it started from. The headline poisoning success rates are not one quantity: storage and execution dissociate, and the early numbers were measured in memory pools that later attack papers describe as unrealistically empty. Four independent 2026 results report the same degradation with no attacker present, which makes attack surface the wrong frame for at least part of the phenomenon. And the claim that nobody separates the trust level of a remembered threat from the trust level of the environment that produced it is false: one paper does exactly that, and the interesting problem is what its solution costs a safety memory in particular. What is not known is the size of any of it. No located source measures how often a safety memory fires on a record it should not trust, and no benchmark evaluates a memory-based guardrail under an attacker who is targeting the guardrail's own memory. The literature search, drafting and citation verification for this paper were carried out with AI assistance under the author's direction. Every citation was machine-verified against the arXiv API and Crossref before inclusion, and every quantitative claim was read back against the cited source's own abstract. The author is responsible for the final text and for all claims made in it.

title: Patterns of Priming in Production: Lexical, Semantic and Structural Alignment in Language Model Generation
abstract: This paper investigates structural priming in language model (LM) production, examining how preceding structural context influences sentence completion. While prior work has demonstrated priming effects in comprehension of structural alternations, it remained unclear whether these persist in production, where, when generating, an LM samples from many possible continuations at each step. We address this question through a series of controlled sentence-completion experiments on dative constructions. In line with prior work, we find that LMs are susceptible to structural priming, particularly in sentences that are semantically coherent. In terms of priming magnitude, we find that while there is a greater relative increase of double-object datives against our baselines, in line with inverse frequency effects, there is a larger absolute increase in prepositional-objects, the more frequently produced construction. Finally, we not only observe that structural priming is boosted by lexico-semantic coherence, but that structurally primed completions display greater levels of lexico-semantic repetition. Taken together, our evidence supports the view that structural priming in LMs operates across multiple levels of linguistic representation, facilitating, and facilitated by syntactic, lexical, and semantic alignment.
